Press Release

Today (13.11.2016) Finance Ministry has reviewed the position regarding availability and
distribution of all denomination of bank notes. Some of the highlights of the review and the decisions
taken are as follows:-

to

6.

10.

Oe

In the first four days ( from November 10" to 13" , upto 5 pm ) about Rs 3.0. lacs crores of old
Rs.500/- and Rs.1000/- bank notes have been deposited in the banking system and about
Rs.50,000 crores has been dispensed to customers by either withdrawal from their accounts or
withdrawal from ATM’s or by exchange at the counter. Within these four days, the banking
system has handled about 18 crore transactions.

Coordination is being continuously done by Ministry of Finance with RBI, Banks and Post
Offices to make all denomination notes available at all locations.

Instructions have been given to the Banks and Post Offices to ensure proper distribution of all
denomination notes. Banks have also been especially advised to ensure the availability and
distribution of small denomination notes.

Chief Secretaries of the States have been requested to identify the rural pockets, if any, where
availability of cash has been a problem and provide all support to the Banks and Post Offices in
order to ensure the last mile distribution of smal! denomination of notes is done through mobile
banking vans and Banking Correspondents (BCs).

It has been reported that certain business houses viz. Hospitals , Caterers , Tent houses etc. are not
accepting Cheques/Demand Drafts and online payment transfer from customers. It 1s advised that
in such cases customer can make a complaint to the concerned District Magistrates/District
Administration for action against such establishments.

Government of Assam has arranged a Mobile Banking Vans with support of Banks and State
Government Staff at certain Hospitals for carrying out emergency banking transactions. All Banks
have now been advised to arrange mobile banking vans to the extent possible at major hospitals to
carry out emergency banking transaction for patients.

Banks have been advised to make arrangements for separate queues for Senior citizens and
Divyang persons. Separate queues will also be arranged for exchange of cash to cash and
transactions against Bank aceSpints.

Government of Arunachal Pradesh has made special arrangements like cash deposits /withdrawal
and opening of new bank accounts in the remotely located areas with the help of Banks and State
Government staff. State Governments have been requested to facilitate opening of new Bank
accounts as a part of financial inclusion programme.

The issuance of the Rs.500/- notes has already commenced.

Banks have been advised to increase the Business Correspondents limit of dispensing cash to
Rs.2500/- for withdrawal from bank accounts.

Banks have been advised to increase the exchange limit over the counter from the existing
Rs.4000/- to Rs.4500/-.

. Banks have been advised to increase the Cash Withdrawal limit at ATMs from the existing

Rs.2000/- to Rs.2500/- per day in the recalibrated ATMs, other ATMs will continue to dispense
Rs.50/- and Rs. 100/- notes until they are recalibrated.

OFFICE MEMORANDUM

Subject: | Recommendations of the 7" Central Pay Commission — bunching of
stages in the revised pay structure under Central Civil Services
(Revised Pay) Rules, 2016.

The undersigned is directed to say that in view of the recommendation of the 7"
Central Pay Commission regarding bunching of stages in the revised pay structure, it has
been decided that in cases where in revision of pay, the pay of Government servants
drawing pay at two or more stages in pre-revised Pay Band and Grade Pay or scale, as
the case may be, get fixed at same Cell in the applicable Level in the new Pay Matrix,
one additional increment shall be given for every two stages bunched and the pay of
Government servant drawing higher pay in pre-revised structure shall be fixed at the next
vertical Cell in the applicable Level.

2. For this purpose, pay drawn by two Government servants in a given Pay Band and
Grade Pay or scale where the higher pay is at least 3% more than the lower pay shall
constitute two stages. Officers drawing pay where the difference is less than 3% shall not
be entitled for this benefit.

3. As per illustration given in para 5.1.37 of the Report of the 7" Central Pay
Commission, if two persons drawing pay of = 53,000 and & 54,590 in the GP 2 10,000
are to be fitted in the new Pay Matrix, the person drawing pay of = 53,000 on
multiplication by a factor of 2.57 will expect a pay corresponding to = 1,36,210 and the
person drawing pay of 2 54,590 on multiplication by a factor of 2.57 will expect a pay
corresponding to = 1,40,296. Revised pay of both should ideally be fixed in the first cell of
Level 14 in the pay of ® 1,44,200 but to avoid bunching the person drawing pay of @
54,590 will get fixed in second cell of Level 14 in the pay of 2 1,48,500.

September, 2014 to look into various aspects of Expenditure Reforms to be undertaken by
the Government. The Ministry of Labour & Employment vide letter No. Z-13025/02/2016SSI dated 2™ September, 2016 has forwarded certain recommendations of the

- Qualifying criteria for bidders

- To put in place the empowered project teams for all large value projects.

- Variation clause to be included in the contract document.

- Use of buy-back facility for standard furniture items and also outsourcing of
services.

procedure for payments to Sellers/Suppliers in Government e-Market Place are required to

and ZTIs. Accordingly, the copies of the Office Memorandums of Ministry of Finance,
Department of Expenditure on the above subject which have been received from Ministry

of Labour & Employment are forwarded herewith for information, guidance and taking

Sub:-Seeding of Aadhaar number in the UAN database of EPF members -
regarding.

Madam / Sir,

It is noted that under the implemented Universal Account Number (UAN)
programme, the seeding of Aadhaar number in the UAN database of EPF members is very
low(just 23% up to 25.10.2016). At present for 7.95 crores UAN issued by EPFO only
around 1.82 crores Aadhar numbers of members have been uploaded and approimately 1.5
crores Aadhaar numbers of members have been digitally verified by the employers.

It needs to be emphasized that to identify the member across his different
employments, the Universal Account Number (UAN) database of members has to be seeded
with his KYC details. The Aadhaar number issued by UIDAI is one of the important KYCs
being seeded to extend a number of direct services to the member.

At PRAGATI Meeting dated 24/08/16, it was pointed out that seeding of Aadhaar
number in the UAN database of EPF members is very low (20%) and OSD(L&E) asked for
timelines for completion of Aadhaar Seeding in view of the poor performance.
Subsequently, Ministry of Labour & Employment has set the timeline to ensure 100%
Aadhaar Seeding in Beneficiary Database by 31/12/2016.

So, field offices may conduct awareness programme regarding benefits of Aadhaar
Seeding and are required to take all necessary steps to complete the task of Seeding of
Aadhaar within given time frame and monitor the same on daily basis.

Aadhaar Seeding will be monitored on weekly basis at Head Office and the
explanation of low progressing offices shall be called.

This is for your information and necessary action.

MINUTES OF THE 4°° MEETING OF THE SUB-COMMITTEE OF THE CENTRAL
BOARD OF TRUSTEES, EPF ON CONTRACT WORKERS
(EPF HEADQUARTER, NEW DELHI, 07" Nov, 2016 at 02:00 P.M.)

The 4" meeting of the Sub-Committee of Central of Trustees, EPF on Contract Workers

was chaired by Dr. V.P. Joy, Central Provident Fund Commissioner. The following members
attended the meeting:-

Shri Shankar Saha : Employees’ Representative

Shri A.D. Nagpal ; Employees’ Representative

Shri K.V. Shekhar Raju : Employers’ Representative

Shri Vinod Kumar : Director, SS, Central Government Representative
Shri M. Narayanappa : ACC-I (Compliance) — Convener

Dr. UD Choubey, Director General, SCOPE could not attend the meeting and was granted
leave of absence.

The list of officers of the Employees’ Provident Fund Organization who attended the
meeting is at Annexure-A.

The Central PE Commissioner & Chairman of the Sub-Committee welcomed the members
to the 4" meeting of the Sub-Committee of CBT, EPF on Contract Workers. CPFC briefly outlined
the number of steps taken by EPFO during the last six months to make the transfer easier for the
contract employees. He emphasized that effort of the EPFO for simplification of the procedures
and providing all the services online should give results. The vision of EPFO to make a system
where things be easy for employees i.e. no transfer required upon change of job and no
certification required from previous employer should be met during this financial year.

Thereafter, the agenda items were taken up.

Item No. I: Confirmation of the minutes of 3 meeting of the Sub-Committee of the
CBT, EPF on Contract Workers held on 2" May, 2016.

The minutes of the 3 meeting of the Sub-Committee of the Central Board of
Trustees, EPF on Contract Workers held on 2" May, 2016 had been circulated to all
members and no comments were received. Accordingly, the minutes of the 3° meeting of
the Sub-Committee of the Central Board of Trustees, EPF on Contract Workers were
approved.

installation of Roof Top Solar (RTS Projects) in Government Building/Premises as these

technical losses.

Public Sector Undertakings for facilitating in the area of Solar Energy and executing the work

has been assigned with the responsibility of facilitating and installing of Roof Top Solar

control of Ministry of Labour and Employment the work in connection with installation of Roof
Top Solar Photovoltaic Panels will be executed by the Rajasthan Electronics and Instrument
Limited.

paid, whether a policy has been adopted to use only LED Lamps, renewable energy used if
any etc.

incorporating changes in the ECR which will be UAN based and also for handling the

Yojana). The changes require proper training to the EPF Officers and staff and also to the
employers.

A facility has also been provided on the EPFO website for the employers to
nominate themselves for the training and the registration has started. The following
plan has been made to cover maximum people for the training in the minimum possible
time. |

Sub: List of activities to be undertaken after shifting of field office functions
on to the PDB-reg.

Madam / Sir,

This has a reference to our earlier letters of even no. dated 97.10.2016 &
07.10.2016 whereby several field offices were brought on central PDBs. Since, the
month of October, 2016, a gradual rollout of activities has commenced towards the
centralisation and consolidation of field office data and functions to the central
database located at Gurgaon. With the gradual moving of such field office database
to central PDBs, there is an urgent need to take certain steps at the field office level
so as to ensure that the change does not being in any sudden abruption or mishap
in any future requirement which may be unforeseen as of now. Accordingly, it is
requested that the following steps may be taken immediately under supervision of
the respective OIC of each field office and a certificate to this effect may be sent by
each office to the Information Service Division at epfo.project@epfindia.gov.in at the
earliest. Hence, the following may be ensured:

a) All the servers in each of the field office which have been in use till now
may be carefully packed and sealed in a manner which would be dust
free and moisture free and safely kept at an isolated place. It may also be
ensured that such detached servers are not brought into use/switched
on by anybody without the express approval of the Officer-In-Charge who
shall do so only after recording the reasons of such a need in writing and
intimating the same to g-NOC, National Data Centre, Dwarka.

b) While the availability of the central servers shall be on a 24X7 basis and
respective offices can access them at all times, it is necessary that all the
switches and routers in the field offices are immediately connected to the
main UPS which shall be kept switched on during all operating hours.

c) It has been noticed that some offices have also put PCs in use in place of
thin clients on the MPLS network for the normal official functioning. It is
accordingly advised that all such PCs are immediately loaded with latest
licensed antivirus software and at the same time it may also be ensured
that the PCs do not get connected to the internet at any point of time

‘while it is on the MPLS grid.

d) It has also been noticed that a significant number of offices have during

€)

the course of time installed several unmanaged switches due to
exigencies of the time. However, such unmanaged switches lead toa
deterioration in performance of the network and may slow down the
systems. Accordingly, it is advised that every office converts all such
unmanaged switches into managed ones at the earliest.

It may also be ensured that all local EDP centres are cleared of any
network clutters and the routers and Switches are kept in dust free
hygienic conditions so that whenever it is visited upon by any external
audit, the systems meet with the proper standards. Every office shall be
put under a physical systems audit very shortly. Accordingly all efforts
may be taken with the help of local technical staff and the UTIITSL
network personnel, wherever available, immediately.

2. It is also requested that if the field offices have any other suggestions to

make or clarifications to seek, the same may be addressed to
epfo. project@epfindia.gov.in.

Thanking you.

member accounts on or before the date of retirement

Regarding pension claims, a copy of PPO should be issued to retiring
member on the date of his /her retirement .

The Officers-in-Charge of all field offices shall personally monitor the
retirement cases on priority and ensure that the above instructions are
implemented fully .

SUB : PRIORITY TO BE GIVEN TO SETTLEMENT OF DEATH CASE CLAIM
SETTLEMENTS WITHIN 7 DAYS- DIRECTIONS GIVEN BY PM DURING
PRAGATI REVIEW MEETING HELD OWN 26.10.2016,

Dear Sir,

The Hon'ble Prime Minister has during the PRAGATI review meeting taken on 26.10.2016
shown his concern regarding delay in settlement of EPF/EPS/EDLI claims especially in Death
Cases.

You are hereby instructed to ensure that all death case claims submitted by spouse/
nominees legal heir of EPF member be invariably settled within a period of 7 days from
date of submission of claim form in concerned field office where the deceased members
accounts are being maintained .

In case of pension claims, where PPO is to be issued from offices other than where the
account of the deceased member is being maintained , the total period taken for settlement of
such claims should also not exceed 7 days . It will be joint responsibility of OICs of both the
concerned offices to issue PPO within 7 days .

The PRO and officials in the Facilitation Centre should be instructed to scrutinise the claim
forms received in respect of death cases and guide the claimants for submission of all required
documents in one attempt only .

For this purpose one official may be trained in the facilitation centre and deputed to look
after death case claims with proper display in this regard made on the seat/counter “Please
contact for death cases” in Hindi,Regional Language and English. .

All death case claims must invariably be stamped as “DEATH CASE-TOP PRIORITY” .

The Officers-in-Charge of all field offices shall personally monitor the death cases on day
to day basis. .

Tours faithfully,

Subject: Next version of UAN and clear the Tasks pending with employers for
confirmation of first time employment/previous employmentregarding.

Madam/Sir,

EPFO is in the process of development and implementation of next version of UAN,
whereby the Universal Account Number of an EPF member is to be obtained/linked with
present employment by the employer before filing the ECR. It is submitted that in the
current process, the employer is to declare about the first time employment of member to
obtain his new UAN or link the UAN or previous member ID in case the new employee has a
previous EPF membership. This happens after the ECR has been submitted by the employer.
The system identifies the new member IDs in the present ECR viz-a-viz previous ECR and
pushes the same to employer portal for declaration. To sensitize the employers about the
next version of UAN, a handout on the silent features of the UAN 2.0 is annexed herewith.

2 It is noted that a large number of tasks are pending with employers for this
declaration. The proposed process under UAN 2.0 requires the allotment of UAN upfront and
the ECR can be filed only in case of such members where UAN has either been allotted to
member or the previous UAN has been linked to his present employment. Presently, the
pending tasks with employers are already available to field offices in the dashboard provided
through Head Office letter No. R-I/P-20/UAN/2014/364/25554-150 dated 27/11/2014
(placed under Office Orders/ Circulars at S. No. 613 of 2014-15). The detailed process flow
is available at www.epfindia.gov.in >>Process Flow for portability & first time employment.

3. It is submitted that the implementation of revised ECR requires that all the
contributing members should have UAN, failing which, the employer would not able to remit
the dues in respect of these members.

4. Accordingly, it is proposed to convey to the employers through all means to carry out
the above activity by 15.11.2016 and clear the pendency.

Salient features of next version of Universal Account Number (UAN)

e The UAN program was launched by EPFO in the year 2014 with an objective to provide one
umbrella number to its members for all the employments of an EPF member with different

establishments.

e Under this program, a number of services were provided to the member namely; updated
passbook, dynamically updated UAN card, SMS services on registered mobile numbers of

activated UANs and portability in case of KYC seeded UANSs etc.

e To take UAN program to the next level of service delivery, there is a need to revise the
processes involved in generation/ linking of UAN of members in his various employments and
its integration with next version of ECR and Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojna (PMRPY)

scheme.
Key features of next version of UAN:
> UAN would be the key field in Electronic Challan cum Return (ECR).

For a member joining EPF for the first time, the UAN would be obtained by the employer or

Vv

member prior to filing of ECR by the employer for that member.

> The employer would furnish the member’s details on the basis of KYC documents i.e.
Aadhaar, PAN, Bank Account etc. to avoid future issues about member’s name, name of

father/spouse, date of birth etc.

> The UAN would be allotted upfront on the portal and would be validated in the ECR file of

the employer at the time of its submission.
‘

> Also for a member who was earlier a member of EPF prior to joining the present
establishment, the linking of the existing UAN of the member should necessarily be done by

the employer before filing of UAN based ECR.

> The member's details as available in the provided UAN i.e. name of member, date of birth,

father’s/ Husband’s name would be used in the ECR of the present employment.
> The generation/linking of UAN can be done through an online functionality on UAN portal.
> This would be mandatory for the employer to include the new members in the ECR.

> The employer may start remitting dues through ECR for the linked UAN thereafter.

Subject:- Release of rent where office is in rental buildings-regarding.

Sir, .

As you are aware, normally before expiry of the lease period a proposal
for extention of lease shall be forwarded to HO through ACC (Zone). However, it
is frequently seen that the proposal for extention of lease are submitted
belatedly. Also, many a times the proposal come directly from the concerned

delays the examination.

not ensuring that the increase shall be maximum of 15% after 5 years or as per
CPWD fair rent certificate whichever is less, and if negotiation fails, action is not
being taken to search alternate office accommodations.

same premises, pending premises extention of lease, rent at existing rate has to
be paid. However, it is seen that at times no rent is released at all in time.

4. Already, new policy is under formulation for regulating the search of new
premises, lease agreement and extention of lease. Therefore, pending the new
policy formation, it is requested that the above points may be kept in mind while
forwarding any proposal for a new lease/ extention of lease.

out on the basis of average emoluments/calculation ceiling, whichever is lower, as per Ministry

Sub: Contribution to pension fund on salary exceeding Rs. 15000 per month with effect
from 1** September 2014 — reg.

Sir/ Madam,

Kind attention is invited to the notification no. GSR- 609 dated 22.08.2014 through
which following provisions were inserted in sub Para 4 of Para 11 of Employees Pension
Scheme 1995 (determination of pensionable salary). The provisions of Para 11 (4) is
reproduced below for your ready reference : -

“The existing members as on the 1% day of September, 2014, who at the option of
the employer and employee, had been contributing on salary exceeding six thousand and
five hundred rupees per month, may on a fresh option to be exercised jointly by the
employer and employee continue to contribute on salary exceeding fifteen thousand rupees
per month :

Provided that the aforesaid members have to contribute at the rate of 1.16 per cent
or salary exceeding fifteen thousand rupees as an additional contribution from and out of
the contributions payable by the employees for each month under the provisions of the Act
on the rules made there under :

Provided further that the fresh option shall be exercised by the member within a
period of six months from the 1° day of September, 2014:

Provided also that the period specified in the second proviso may, on sufficient cause
being shown by the member, be extended by the Regional Provident Fund Commissioner for
a further period not exceeding six months:

Provided also that if no option is exercised by the member within such period
(including the extended period), it shall be deemed that the member has not opted for
contribution over wage ceiling and the contributions to the Pension fund made over the
wage ceiling in respect of the member shall be diverted to the Provident Fund account of
the member along with interest as declared under the Employees’ Provident Fund Scheme
from time to time.”

In order to examine the compliance status by the field offices with respect to the
above notification and modification, details in respect of employees contributing to the
pension fund exceeding salary of Rs.15000 per month have been analysed. Following facts
have surfaced on analysis of the details as above for the month of April and May 2016.

All RO/SROs are therefore advised that each case of contribution on salary exceeding

Status report in respect of such employees in each office and action taken by these

Subject : Proper handling of cases before Consumer Forums - regarding

Reference: This office Circular No. LC-9(12)2013/CPFC Ref/Pt/3865
dated 16.5.2014 (available at S.No.118) , Circular No. LC2(990)2015/MH/10588 dated 12.06.2015

Sir/Madam,

Please refer to this office circulars referred to above vide which comprehensive
guidelines on handling of legal cases were issued.

2. It is observed that inspite of detailed instructions on handling of the Consumer
Forum Cases, the performance of field offices in defending cases before Consumer forum
is not very encouraging and the offices are not following the directions in true spirit.

3: It is also a matter of serious concern that there is a steep rise in number of
consumer forum cases. But, the cases are not being defended properly at the level of
District Forums leading to passing of adverse orders by District Forum which are rarely
reversed by Appellate Courts and set a bad precedent for other cases. It is pertinent to
mention that these cases are mostly related to deficiency in service/claim settlement/
Pension scheme and, therefore, can not be neglected.

4. Needless to say, there is urgent requirement to focus attention on the Consumer
Forum cases and to ensure that the department is defended effectively in these cases.

5. Zonal ACCs and RPFC/OICs must review the status of Consumer Forum cases
personally atleast twice a month. It should be ensured that proper written
statement/Counter Reply is filed in each case describing the relevant provision of Act
and Scheme. The Forum should also be apprised of the mandate of the Act and be
requested to pass orders as per prescribed provisions.

6. It is reiterated that the above circulars should scrupulously be followed by the
field functionaries for meticulous handling of all legal cases in their jurisdiction.

Yours faithfully,

(Dr. S.K. Thakur)
Addl. Central P. F. Commissioner (Legal)

The Modified Assured Career Progression Scheme was introduced with effect from
01.09.2008 in pursuance of the recommendations of the Sixth Pay Commission by this
Department’s OM No.35034/3/2008-Estt(D) dated 19" May, 2009. Subsequently,
clarifications/ FAQs were issued vide OM dated 16.11.2009, 09.09.2010, 01.04.2011,
13.06.2012, 04.10.2012 and 10.12.2014. These instructions are in force with effect from
01.09.2008.

recommended inter-alia as follows:

“MACP will continue to be administered at 10, 20 and 30 years as before. In the
new Pay Matrix, the employee will move to immediate next level in hierarchy.
Fixation of pay will follow the same principle as that for a regular promotion in the
Pay Matrix. MACPS will continue to be applicable to all employees up to Higher
Administrative Grade (HAG) level except members of Organised Group ‘A’
Services.”

3. The Government has considered the above recommendation and has accepted the
same. In the light of the recommendations of the 7” CPC accepted by the Government, the
Modified Assured Career Progression Scheme (MACPS) will continue to be administered at
10, 20 and 30 years as before. Further, Para | and 2 of the existing Scheme (Annexure to
this Department's OM No. 35024/3/2008-Estt.D dated 19" May, 2009) will be substituted
by the following words:-

“|. There shall be three financial upgradations under the MACPS as per TOC
recommendations, counted from the direct entry grade on completion of 10, 20 and
30 years services respectively or 10 years of continuous service in the same level in
Pay Matrix, whichever is earlier.

2. The MACPS envisages merely placement in the immediate next higher level
in the Pay Matrix as given in PART A of Schedule of the CCS (Revised Pay) Rules,
3016. Thus, the level in the Pay Matrix at the time of financial upgradation under

interactions.

review of Inspection Reports found that in several cases Interim Reports are uploaded by the
Enforcement Officers which are in fructuous in nature. In view of this, it is directed that:

facility for the edit.

Sub: Contribution to pension fund on salary exceeding Rs. 15000 per month with effect
from 1* September 2014 — reg.

Sir/ Madam,

Kind attention is invited to the notification no. GSR- 609 dated 22.08.2014 through
which following provisions were inserted in sub Para 4 of Para 11 of Employees Pension
Scheme 1995 (determination of pensionable salary). The provisions of Para 11 (4) is
reproduced below for your ready reference : -

“The existing members as on the 1* day of September, 2014, who at the option of
the employer and employee, had been contributing on salary exceeding six thousand and
five hundred rupees per month, may on a fresh option to be exercised jointly by the
employer and employee continue to contribute on salary exceeding fifteen thousand rupees
per month:

Provided that the aforesaid members have to contribute at the rate of 1.16 per cent
or salary exceeding fifteen thousand rupees as an additional contribution from and out of
the contributions payable by the employees for each month under the provisions of the Act
on the rules made there under :

Provided further that the fresh option shall be exercised by the member within a
period of six months fromthe day of September, 2014:

Provided also that the"period specified in the second proviso may, on sufficient cause
being shown by the member, be extended by the Regional Provident Fund Commissioner for
a further period not exceeding six months:

Provided also that if no option is exercised by the member within such period
(including the extended period), it shall be deemed that the member has not opted for
contribution over wage ceiling and the contributions to the Pension fund made over the
wage ceiling in respect of the member shall be diverted to the Provident Fund account of
the member along with interest as declared under the Employees’ Provident Fund Scheme
from time to time.”

In order to examine the compliance status by the field offices with respect to the
above notification and modification, details in respect of employees contributing to the
pension fund exceeding salary of Rs.15000 per month have been analysed. Following facts
have surfaced on analysis of the details as above for the month of April and May 2016.

Sub: Non adherence to the instructions for sanction and disbursement of pension under
EPS, 1995 by field offices — reg.

Sir/ Madam,

Instances have been brought to the notice of the Head Office regarding the fraudulent
payments made in some of the offices in the sanction and disbursement of pension to the
members of Employees Pension Scheme 1995.

CPFC has taken strong view on such cases of fraudulent payments occurred in some of
the offices.

Prima facie it has been observed that the reported fraudulent payments have taken place
due to non adhering of the existing instructions and manual of Accounting Procedure
Employees’ Pension Scheme, 1995 Part-IV in settlement and disbursement of pension. It has
also been observed that it is the failure on the part of officer in-charge of the concerned field
offices who have failed to monitor and ensure strict compliance of the instructions issued on the
procedure for settlement and disbursement of pension leading to such fraudulent payments.

Investigations are..being made for all such reported fraudulent payments by the
concerned divisions and necessary actions will be taken against all concerned by the competent
authority. Steps are also being under taken to examine the reasons for occurrence of such
fraudulent payments for making changes/ improvements in the existing system. Till such time
changes/improvements in the system of settlement of pension and disbursement are finalized
all officers-in- charge are requested to ensure following actions with immediate effect.

1. All the existing instructions including manual on Employees Pension Scheme 1995 must
be followed strictly.

2. A hard copy should be sent to bank for details of BRS with CD and must be properly
authenticated.

3. Regarding change of date of birth of EPS members, the instructions issued, vide
communication no.Pension/3(8)OR/1/2005/69869 dated 12.12.2006 should be followed
with following additional safeguards till further instructions in this regard :-

i. For such cases of change in date of birth the member must have Aadhar linked
activated UAN;

li. | The request for change in date of birth must have approval of RPFC in charge of
the Region.

4. The request for change of bank account of pensioner should be entertained only with
Aadhar linked activated UAN.

Officer-in-charge of field offices are advised to have frequent check at all levels of
process flow on the settlement and disbursement of pension and ensure that short comings
found are rectified immediately. If any fraudulent Payment on disbursement of pension takes
place, henceforth, officer in-charge of the office will be held primarily responsible for such
lapses,

Addl. CPFCs (Zone) are requested to monitor the system and procedure being followed
on pension settlement by the offices under their jurisdiction at regular interval and take suitable
actions instantly.

Yours faithfully,

Vols,

Sir,

Whereas Ms. Pinky has made a request in writing vide her application dated 20.08.2016 for
obtaining information under Section 6(1) of the RTI Act, 2005.

under Section 5(1) of the said Act is required to consider and provide the information within 30
days of the receipt of the request.

3. And whereas Section 5(4) of the Act provides the Central Public Information Officer may
seek the assistance of any other officer as he considers it necessary for the proper discharge of his
duties. Sub-section (5) further provides that any officer whose assistance has been sought shall
render all assistance to the Central Public Information Officer. In the event a complaint is made by
the applicant is referred “for the purposes of any contravention of the provisions of the Act, such
other officer shall be treated as Central Public Information Officer” and may be liable for penalties
under Section 20 of the said Act. Further in the event of violation of provisions/non-furnishing of
documents/information such an officer is liable for penalties under Section 20(1) of the Act @
Rs.250/- for each day of delay which may extend upto Rs. 25,000/-.

4. And whereas under Section 6(3) of Right to Information Act, it has been provided that:
“Where an application is made to a public authority requesting for an information:-

(i) which is held by another public authority; or

(ii) the subject matter of which is more closely connected with the functions of another
public authority.

the public authority, to which such application is made, shall transfer the application or such part of

it as may be appropriate to that other public authority and inform the applicant immediately about
such transfer,”

Sub: Project Monitoring Committee (PMC) in respect of EPFO’s construction works.
Sir/Madam,

Please refer to this office circular No.CS-3(4) Sub Committee on B&C/2016/3257-59 dated
11.5.2016 (copy enclosed for ready reference).

As may be seen, the Project Monitoring Committee (PMC) is empowered only for monitoring of
the works being done by Public Work Organization (PWO) at periodical intervals ensuring that the work is
being done by the PWO in accordance with Rules and Procedures prescribed in the PWO.

The Committee is not empowered for any escalation of cost/deviation/change from the
sanctioned scope of work as per the prescribed procedure. Any deviation or alternation or escalation of cost
requires to be placed before the Competent Authority i.e. Executive Committee of CBT.

Accordingly, it is once again advised that a Project Monitoring Committee for the construction
projects in compliance of direction given in letter dated 11.5.2016 may be constituted in accordance with
Rule 133 of GFR. In this regard, if possible non —official members of the Building & Construction Sub
Committee from the respective area may also be invited as per their convenience. It is also clarified that
where the construction work is taking place in Sub Regional Office, the OIC shall be made a member of
PMC.

Action Taken Report in this regard may please be sent by 14" of Oct’2016.

Subject: Monitoring of the Projects —regarding.
Sir,

The Sub-Committee of the Executive Committee, CBT, EPF on Building &
Construction in its meeting No.1 held on 24 March 2016 noted the present status of on
going construction projects and decided that proper monitoring of the projects must be
ensured for timely completion ensuring quality and full compliance of relevant rules and
regulations including the provisions of EPF & MP Act, 1952 in respect of construction
workers engaged on the projects.

: This issue was also discussed in a meeting held with CPWD and NBCC on

5.5.2016 at Head Office wherein the CPWD officers informed that the rules and
procedures to be followed for execution of construction projects are already laid down
in GFR Rules 133. The relevant rule is reproduced as under:

Rule 133: For original works and repair works entrusted to a ‘Public Works
Organisation’ as defined in Rule 126(2), the administrative approval and
expenditure sanction shall be accorded and funds allotted by the concerned
authority under these rules and in accordance with the delegation of Financial
Power Rules 1978. The Public Works Organisation shall then execute the work
entrusted to it in accordance with the rules and procedures prescribed in that
organization.

Accordingly, all ACCs(Zones) are requested to constitute a Project Monitoring
Committee to be chaired by ACC(Zone) with RPFC-I of the Region, RPFC-II(FA) of
the Region and technical staff ie. JE/AE of Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation
in the Region/Zone as members. The OIC of the SRO may also be co-opted, if
required. The Committee in accordance with Rule 133 of GFR may ensure that
execution of the work by the PWO is being done in accordance with Rules and
Procedures prescribed in the PWO. As the PWO in most of the cases is CPWD, the
CPWD Manual available on net, may please be referred to by the Committee. Any

gaps and irregularities noticed may be immediately taken up with the PWO for course
correction.

Subject: Implementation of Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojna(PMRPY) - regarding.
Madam/Sir,

Please refer to Head Office letter No. R-I/PMRPY/2016/499 dated 12.09.2016 on the subject
cited above. In this regard, it is informed that the PMRPY portal has been activated for registration of
employers and members for the implementation of the said Scheme. It is reiterated that the
Government of India has designed the Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojna (PMRPY) to incentivise
employment generation.

2. Under this Scheme the Government of India would pay 8.33% of the EPS contribution of the
employer for the new employment provided, there is an increase in employment in that
establishment. It may be recalled that the copy of guidelines of the Scheme duly notified by Ministry
of Labour & Employment has already been circulated vide this office letter dated 12/09/2016 through
e-mail.

convenience of employers. The documents have also been placed on EPFO website
www.epfindia.gov.in >> Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojna >> Login. The Standard Operating
Procedure (SOP) document is also enclosed for awareness of the officers and staff of the Organisation
so that the queries raised by employers can be addressed during the course of implementation of the
Scheme at your levels as well.

4. In continuation to the earlier instructions issued vide letter dated 12/09/2016, it is once again
requested to publicise the Scheme guidelines and ensure awareness among the officers and staff to
guide the employers about the Scheme guidelines. Maximum efforts should be taken to ensure that
all the eligible employers avail the benefits of this Scheme without any hassles. The Hindi version
would follow.

Please refer to this office circulars dated 19.04.2016 & 21.04.2016 (website sl no. 42 & 47)
regarding the conduct of the Fifth APFC (DR) Probationary examination at NATRSS from 27" June to 1°"
July , 2016.

2) As per the EPF (Probationary) Examination Scheme, General Category candidates have to obtain
minimum 45 % marks in each paper and SC/ST Category candidates have to obtain minimum 40% marks
in each paper to pass the Probationary Examination. Thus candidates who are absent in even one paper
or those who do not get the minimum qualifying marks in even one paper are considered as ‘FAIL’ in the
examination and will have to appear for the same again. However candidates who have failed to qualify
in the examination but have secured 50% and above in any one of the papers will be granted exemption
in that paper and will not have to appear in that paper in the next examination.

3: The result of the examination has been prepared as per the above Scheme and is enclosed for
information of all and is subject to outcome of changes due to re-totalling and verification of marks etc.
Those candidates who have failed in the examination and are required to appear for one or more papers
may be directed to attend the next Probationary Examination. It is requested that all the concerned
candidates may be intimated about the result and directed to appear for the next Probationary
Examination when the same is conducted.

enclosed with circular dated 19.04.2016 ( website circular no. 42), facility is provided for candidates who

Sub: Submission of Revised Estimates for the year 2016-17 and
Budget Estimates for the year 2017-18 in respect of Employees’
Provident Funds Scheme, 1952 (including Employees’ Pension

Scheme, 1995) and Employees’ Deposit-Linked Insurance
Scheme, 1976.

In accordance with the provisions regarding budget contained in Para 58
of the EPF Scheme 1952, on probable Receipts and Expenditure relating to the
Administration of the Funds, the Revised Estimates for the year 2016-17 and
the Budget Estimates for the year 2017-18 of the EPF Organisation, based on
the actual Income & Expenditure upto 30°" September 2016 (i.e. from
1.04.2016 to 30.9.2016), are to be prepared and placed before the Central

Board of Trustees, EPF for consideration and approval in this financial year.

2: The budgetary exercise may not be treated as mere routine exercise and
it should receive the personal attention of the Regional P.F. Commissioner-I
and the OIC of SRO for its correctness and timely submission. On the part of
the RPFC-II (F&A), it should be treated as a vital function for the respective
Region including for the SROs and he/she should devote his/her personal
attention in assisting the Regional Commissioner in-charge of the Region.
Regional Offices may frame the BE/RE with due care as per provisions in GFRs
after assessing the actual needs of the regions. It has been observed that in
the last five years, RE was more than BE but the actual expenditure was even
less than the BE for a few regions. Therefore, due care may be taken while
submitting the estimates to H.O. Further, RE may be projected in such a
manner to obviate the need for re- appropriation in the last quarter of the

financial year.

3. PDUNASS shall be treated as an independent unit and separate funds
are allotted to meet its own expenditure and the Zonal Training Institutes
(ZTIs), Sub-ZTI (Shillong) working under it. As such, Director, PDUNASS,
may submit budget proposal separately for PDUNASS including ZTIs and the
Sub-ZTI. The budget for Deputy Director, Vigilance (NZ) may be included in
the proposal of PDUNASS.

4. ACC (ASD), Head Office is also required to submit the proposal of
Revised Estimates 2016-17 & Budget Estimates 2017-18 in respect of Head
Office including the proposal of National Data Centre, Bhavishya Nidhi Enclave
and Bhavishya Nidhi Bhawan regarding requirement of funds under the budget
head “Minor Works” which will be at the disposal of Chief Engineer, Head
Office.

5; Similarly, the EPF Appellate Tribunals, Delhi & Bengaluru shall be treated
as separate units and separate funds are to be allotted to meet its own
expenditure. As such, Registrar, EPF Appellate Tribunal, Delhi & Bengaluru
may submit budget proposals separately.

6, The following guidelines may please be kept in mind while formulating
the Revised Estimates for 2016-17 and Budget Estimates for 2017-18: -

(i) One single proposal is required to be prepared in respect of a Region as
a whole by consolidating the proposals of Regional Office and the SubRegional Offices. RPFC-In-Charge of the Region as well as RPFC-II (F&A)
may, therefore, consult the OICs of SROs under their control
immediately to ensure that there is no delay in transmission of the
requisite information to their office. The Revised Estimates for 2016-17
and Budget Estimates for 2017-18 for the offices of Addl. CPFCs (Zones)
and Permanent Inquiry Officers, Zonal Audit Parties and Deputy
Directorates (Vigilance) may include any new requirements, if any, other
than the routine items like Pay & Allowances, TA, Stationery, Phone etc.
to the Regional Offices or PDUNASS as the case may be, where these
offices are situated, which in turn, will include the same in the

consolidated budget proposal of the Regiorf.

Sub: Merger of UANs - Reg.
Sir/Madam,

It is noted that in some cases, though Universal Account Numbers have been allotted
legitimately i.e. under the prescribed criteria, interventions are necessitated due to following
reasons:-

a) At the time of initial allotment, the employer has not furnished the date of exit in the
ECR although the member has left the employment and joined some other
establishment. Under the defined criteria, two UANs have resulted to such members
for both the employments.

b) At the time of joining the present employment, a new UAN has been allotted to the
member due to wrong declaration by member/ employer under UAN programme.

2. The matter has been examined and it has been decided that in case of duplicate
UANs issued to one EPF member as mentioned above, the following solutions are detailed
below: '

e The members should be advised to apply for P.F. transfer from previous EPF account
to the present EPF account.

e The system would identify such cases on periodic basis where the P.F. transfer has
been effected from one EPF account to another, both having different UANs attached
to these EPF accounts.

e All such identified UANs, from which P.F. transfer has been effected to P.F. account
having different UAN, would be deactivated (the mobile number would be released
by the system for use by the member) and UAN would be blocked for further use.
This would be done in respect of all identified UANs even when no request has been
received from the member.

e The previous member ID would henceforth be linked to the new UAN.

e The member would be informed of the deactivated status of his previous UAN in
case of activated UANs) by SMS to the registered mobile number. He would be
requested to activate the new UAN to get the updated status of his EPF account.

e There is a possibility of arrears payments by the previous employer for the member.
In such cases, since the system knows the new UAN against the deactivated UAN,
the system would automatically populate the new UAN in the ECR (on punching of
previous UAN or member ID by the employer) and the statutory contribution by the
employer against the arrears can be remitted against new UAN only.

3. It is requested that the above process may be informed to the employers and EPF
members, in case there are cases of multiple UANs allotted to same EPF members.

4. This issues with the approval of Central P.F Commissioner.

Yours faithfully,

The undersigned is directed to refer to this Department's O.M. of even No. dated

Kashmir (J&K) and Andaman & Nicobar Islands (A&N) is extended for a further period of
two years w.e.f. 26" September, 2016 subject to the following conditions:

(a) Travel by air to continue to be performed by Air India in Economy class at LTC-80
fare or less.

(b) For journey by air to Jammu & Kashmir, travel by any airline is allowed, however,
the journey should be undertaken in Economy class at a fare less than or equal to
LTC-80 fare of Air India.

(c) The condition that air tickets can be purchased either directly from the airlines
(booking counters/website) or through authorized agents only viz., ‘M/s Balmer
Lawrie and Co. Ltd.’, ‘M/s Ashok Travels and Tours Ltd.’ and ‘IRCTC’ (to the
extent IRCTC is authorized as per DoPT's O.M. No. 31011/6/2002-Estt.(A) dated
02.12.2009), shall necessarily apply.

(d) Efforts should be made by the Government servants to book the ait tickets at the
cheapest fare possible. All the Ministries/ Departments are advised to bring it to the
notice of all their employees that any misuse of LTC will be viewed seriously and
the employees will be liable for appropriate action under the rules. In order to keep
a check on any kind of misuse of LTC, Ministries/ Departments are advised to
randomly get some of the air tickets submitted by the officials verified from the
Airlines concerned with regard to the actual cost of air travel vis-a-vis the cost

indicated on the air tickets submitted by the officials.

2. All other conditions prescribed in this Department's O.M. of even no. dated

26.09.2014 shall continue to apply.

exemption by the appropriate government to protect the interest of the members.

Sub: Forwarding of details required for assessment and timely declaration of

Sir/Madam,
Please refer to the above said subject.

The work relating to the assessment of Productivity Linked Bonus for the year 201516 has been taken up. The Productive Linked Bonus (PLB) for the employees of EPFO is
assessed on the basis of the productivity achieved and manpower used in respect of each
Regional Office separately. For Head Office (including PDUNASS), it is worked out based on
average of All India Productivity and Manpower. Information relating to parameters and
performance as per the Scheme is to be furnished in the Annexure A to C (copies
enclosed).

A NTS ASH

2. During the year 2015-16 (w.e.f. 03.08.2015), time-limit of 20 days (calendar days)
has been notified for settlement of PF, EPS and EDLI claims, transfer and advances cases.
In case, the job is not completed within 20 days, weightage would be reduced for the work
done beyond 20 days. Date of receipt of claim form (complete in all respect) and the date
of dispatch of cheque/transfer through NEFT would be taken into account for reckoning 20
calendar days.

3. As regards issue of “Annual Statement of Accounts”, it has been classified into two
groups, Viz. (1) current year’s Accounts slips issued and (2) Previous year’s Accounts slips
issued during the current year. Accounts slips relating to the “current Year” and those
pertaining to previous years but issued during the current year should be shown separately.

ENFORCEMENT & DAMAGES
4. The activities of “Enforcement & Damages” include:

(1) No. of 7A notices issued.

(2) No. of Speaking Orders of 7A passed and compliance effected.

(3) No. of Speaking Orders passed for Levy of Damages.

(4) No. of Recovery Certificates Executed:-
(a) For default in all the five Accounts (A/c No. 1,2,10,21 & 22)
(b) For default in 3 or 4 of the five Accounts.
(c) For default in 1 or 2 of the five Accounts.

7-A NOTICES

5. Only one notice has to be taken into account for all the three Schemes. In case
three separate notices are issued for the three Schemes, it has to be taken as one only.
Further, only the initial notice issued has to be taken into account and not the notices
issued every time after adjournment of proceedings due to any reason. With the
amendment of Section 7A, the RPFCs are required to decide not only the quantum of dues
but also to decide the Applicability. In such cases also if more than one notices are issued,
it should be taken as one only for the purpose of PLB return.

SPEAKING ORDERS OF 7A PASSED AND COMPLIANCE EFFECTED

6. Against this item all the speaking orders passed under Section 7A should not be
shown. Only those orders passed, which have been complied with, should be shown.
However, instructions contained in the preceding para as “7A Notices” should also be kept
in view.

SPEAKING ORDERS FOR LEVY OF DAMAGES

7. All the speaking orders passed for levy of Damages may be shown against this item.
However, if separate orders are passed for all the three schemes, only one order should be
taken into account for the purpose of Bonus return.

RECOVERY CERTIFICATES EXECUTED

8. Only those Recovery Certificates, which have been duly executed and not merely
issued, should only be shown against this item. This item has been classified into three

Sir/Madam,

Various references were received by this office informing that PF settlement
amounts forwarded to the member’s Jandhan Bank A/c were being rejected by the bank
for the reason that Jandhan Bank A/c has got a credit limit of Rs.1,00,000/- and no
transaction, debit/credit, beyond that limit is allowed in this account. The matter was
taken up with Ministry of Finance to relax the conditions imposed on the bank accounts
opened in ‘Pradhan Mantri Jandhan Yojna (PMJDY)’

Z It has been clarified by the Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance,
Government of India that PMJDY envisage opening of ‘Basic Savings Bank Deposit
Accounts (BSBDA)’. BSBD Accounts inter-alia, have following minimum common
facilities to all customers:

; The account shall not have the requirement of any minimum balance.

ii, The services available in the account will include deposit and withdrawal of cash at
bank branch as well as ATMs; receipt/credit of money through electronic payment
channel or by means of deposit/collection of cheques drawn by Central/State
Government agencies and departments;

iii, While there will no limit on number of deposits that can be made in a month,
account holders will be allowed a maximum of four withdrawals in a month,
including ATM withdrawals; and

iv. Facility of ATM card or ATM-cum-Debit card.

3, However, those persons who do not have any of the ‘officially valid documents’ as

stipulated by RBI, can open “small accounts” with banks. A “Small Accounts” can be

opened on the basis of a self attested photograph and putting her/his signature or thumb
print in the presence of an official of the bank. Such accounts have limitation regarding
the aggregate credits (not more than Rs. One lakh in a year), aggregate withdrawals (not
more than Rs.10,000/- in a month) and balance in the accounts (not more than
Rs.50,000/- at any point of time).

4. It has, accordingly, been advised by the Department of Financial Services, MoF,
GOI that the beneficiaries of EPFO having Small Accounts may be asked to follow
‘KYC/eK YC’, as stipulated by RBI to banks for conversion of their Small Accounts to
Basic Savings Bank Deposit Accounts, which has no such limit/restrictions.

3. In view of above, all Regional/Sub-Regional Offices are advised to inform EPFO
subscribers accordingly to facilitate efficient electronic services.

Subject : Verification of Closed Exempted/Relaxed Establishments - Regarding.
Sir,

Please refer to the subject cited above. Recently a reference was received from a field office
seeking approval of Head Office for taking over of Trust fund of an exempted establishment reported to be
lying closed for more than 14 years. The establishment was also reported to have undergone
merger/acquisition in the past. The Trust had been running illegally all these years.

Z Funds lying with a private Provident Fund Trust where the establishment which was granted
exemption/ relaxation, but is lying closed since long and the Trust is running illegally cannot be said to be
safe and in the interests of the employees. Neither it is the intention of the legislation behind grant of
exemption to the establishments. Such Trust funds may be vulnerable to potential frauds. _In the interest
of the workers and the public, it is desirable that accumulations of the members lying in such private
Provident Fund Trusts is transferred to the statutory fund alongwith past accumulation statement. Due
procedure laid down for transfer of Trust funds may be followed scrupulously. It also needs to be ensured
by the RPFC that liability should not arise on EPFO.

3 Therefore RPFCs of the field offices are directed to take stock of the situation in their respective
jurisdictions and initiate suitable action if any such case comes to notice. An action taken report in this
regard may please be furnished to the Head Office with status note in detail in respect of each
establishment latest by 30.09.2016.

Sub: - Changes in Shram Suvidha Portal- Regarding.

Madam /Sir,

The Unified Shram Suvidha Portal was developed to facilitate reporting of Inspections,
and submission of Returns. This has been envisaged as a single point of contact between
employer, employee and enforcement agencies bringing in transparency in their day-to-day
interactions. Recently some changes have been made in the Shram Suvidha Portal to further
improve its functioning and facilitate the field offices. The changes are as follows:

1. Re-assignment of the Expired task of Inspection due to transfer of EO or his
superannuation/resignation.

a) The link to re-assign the expired tasks of Inspection has been provided in the
Shram Suvidha Portal and the Regional Head Role user through his login may
select the list for the Expired Inspections from the Inspection function and reassign them to another EO giving the reason that the change is due to transfer
or due to the reason that the EO has left service.

b) Once the task is re-assigned, then the same will appear before the Enforcement
Officer to whom it is given and he can now do the work as a fresh case.

c) The EOs may also be instructed that those who have actually completed the
Inspection work should upload the IR before in case of leaving service or
transfer and before their role is de-activated or their jurisdiction has changed.

2. The generation of the LIN against the new registrations taking place happens after
a process of the system based de-duplication on the portal and another set of
1,17,000 code numbers have been ceded with LINs. However in the de- duplication
process 13,469 cases have been found to be almost matching with the already
available LIN mostly with coverage under ESIC. These have to be manually decided
by the Regional Head Role as was done earlier by them in April 2015.

a) To facilitate this a role of Verifier has also been created and the role can be
created by the Regional Heads and they can also do the de-duplication work.
So it is requested to complete this work of de-duplication.

b) The task ranges from 1 to 2,027 and only one office Delhi North has 2027
cases while 33 offices have 100 to 800 cases while remaining are having
less than 100 cases. So with the use of three or four verifiers the task can

be completed and a report then can be given to the CAIU, Head Office. (A
list of such cases is attached)

3. The LIN generation and the de-duplication done earlier by the system and
manually, finally required the confirmation by the employer and so a link for the
verification of the LIN data particularly the data whether the same LIN is correctly
linked to ESIC, EPFO number and other acts, has been provided to the Employers
under their login.

a) The employers can change certain data like their contact details etc. but in
case they want to change the data of name, address, registration number
etc., the task for the confirmation goes to the role of the Verifier and the
Regional Head of the Enforcement Agency based on whose data the LIN was
generated and until he approves the data is not updated on the portal.

b) The employers have already started updating the data and 1,110 cases
have been submitted. The Regional Heads themselves or through the role
of Verifier created from their login can verify the cases and complete the
task.

A user manual for the purpose is available in the login of each role under the link
for downloads.

4. Change of jurisdiction of any Regional Head/Enforcement Officer: The login of a
Regional Head, MIS Role, Verifier or Inspector is created on the Portal as follows:

a) Regional Head: By the Nodal Officer for the Enforcement Agency (at present
RPFC, NDC is having this role and is also the member of Project Steering
Committee of the Portal at the MOL&E. )

b) MIS Role: By the Nodal officer

c) Verifier: By the Regional Head

d) Enforcement Officer: By the Regional Head

The creator of the roles can also de-activate the user when he has left service or
is no more having the task. This is done based on the request received from the
offices for the cases of the Regional Head or the MIS Role.When an officer (having
any of the role) is transferred and gets some role in the new office, the jurisdiction
change can be done by the nodal officer.

This is for your information and necessary action.

Gautam Dixit
Regional P.F. Commissioner-I (CAIU)

The arrears of Provident Fund and allied dues has shown an increasing trend and
therefore the issue assumes great importance and concern for EPFO. The performance in
recovery of current and arrear dues is far below the targets fixed by the Headquarters
which needs immediate correction.

2. The all India Performance upto the month of June, 2016 as per Annual Business
Plan Shows poor performance of recovery which is a matter of great concern.

3. In order to augment recovery, it has been decided that a Special Recovery Drive
will be carried out in the month of September, 2016 (for both Un-Exempted and
Exempted Sector).

viz. details of bank accounts, details of sundry debtors etc. from the records

Department, Inspector of Factories and Boilers’, Inspector of Shops and
Establishments, Employees’ State Insurance Corporation, Regional Transport

opening balance, cases initiated and disposed during the period (Zone-wise) is enclosed for reference

please.

proposed that henceforth the disposal percentage of 7A cases may also be made an indicator of the
ranking given to a RO/SRO in EPFO E.Samiksha. The percentage of 7A enquiries disposed will be the

performance parameter.

4. Accordingly, all OICs are requested to ensure that the 7A cases are properly examined and
reviewed to ensure prompt disposal without any un-necessary and unjustified delays.

Sir,

As per the directions of Headquarters letter dated 28.06.2016, Pandit Deendayal
Upadhyaya National Academy of Social Security (PDUNASS) has organized a training programme
on “Finance & Investment” to be conducted at IIM, Bangalore from 01** Nov -04" Nov
2016 (Four days). One day of Action Learning Projects presentations will be held in the
first week of January 2017 at PDUNASS.

The Aim of the programme is to cover the following areas:

1. Financial Market Index —based overview, Primary market, secondary market and
derivatives, Debt market/Money market —basic overview, corporate debt, PSU Bonds, Gsec, Treasury Bills, call Money, Commercial Bills, Commercial papers, Certificate of
Deposit and Term Money.

2. Fixed Income Terminologies, Pricing and Yield, Yield risk management, structured
products, yield curve analysis, Bond Math, ratio analysis & Credit rating.

3. Data Analysis-how markets react to different data releases and events like, Budget, IIP
No’s Inflation, Monetary Policy.

4. Portfolio Management -trading strategies, Measuring volatility, Risk and_ return,
calculation of Beta and Standard Deviation.

5. ETF/Equity —basic overview, ETF Structure, Risk/Rewards and dependence on Market
factors, comparative analysis.

The list of participants duly approved by CPFC for the above mentioned training
programme is enclosed herewith.

All the concerned OICs are therefore requested to relieve the officers posted in their
Regional/Sub Regional offices with the directions to report for the training programme at IIM,

Dear Sir/ Madam,




The Government of India, Ministry of Personal, Public Grievances & Pensions,
Department of Pension & Pensioners’ Welfare vide OM No 38/37/2016-P&PW(A) (i) dated
04.08.2016 conveyed that in pursuance of Government’s decision on the recommendation of
the Seventh Central Pay Commission, the President is pleased to introduce the modifications in
the rules regulating pension, Retirement/Death/Service Gratuity, Family Pension, disability
pension, ex-gratia lump sum compensation, etc. under the CCS (Pension) Rules, 1972 and
Computation of Pension under CCS (Computation of Pension) Rules, 1981, CCS (Extraordinary
Pension), Rules, 1939 etc. These revised provisions shall apply to Government servants who
retire/die in harness on or after 01.01.2016 (copy attached as Annexure ‘A’).

2.
The Ministry of Finance further vide its OM no. 38/37/2016-P&PW(A) (ii) dated 4th
August, 2016 conveyed the sanction of the President to the regulation with effect from
01.01.2016 of pension/family pension of all the pre-2016 pensioners/family pensioners in the
indicated manner. (copy attached as Annexure ‘B’.)

3.
In this regard, it is informed that the Central Board of Trustees, EPF in its 214th
meeting held on 26th July, 2016 adopted the notification on resolution of the Government of
India accepting the 7th Central Pay Commission's recommendations. The Central Board also
resolved to adopt any other notification that will be issued by the Government of India in due
course for the Officers and employees of the Central Board.

4.
The State Bank of India has been disbursing pension to pensioners of Central
Government and they are well conversant with the process of revising pension. Though EPFO
do not come under this arrangement and since the State Bank of India is also disbursing
pension to our pensioners, all the Officers Incharge are requested to take up the issue with
the respective link branches to allow the revised pension payments without issuing individual
revised PPOs and orders relating to arrear payments. It may be ensured that the State Bank
of India revises the payment of pension and payment of arrears to our pensioners in the
manner they do for Central Government Pensioners in accordance with the instructions issued
by Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pension, Department of Pension and
Pensioners Welfare, Government of India. It may further be ensured that the pensions are
revised and arrears are paid to the pensioners by 31.08.2016.

The requisition for additional budget, if any, may be sent to FA & CAO to meet the
expenditure involved in making the payment of arrears.

6.
The PPOs of each pensioner be revised and revised PPOs be sent to the Pension
Paying Bank. This task be completed in a time bound manner. The entire exercise be

OFFICE MEMORANDUM

Subject: Provisional Seniority List of Data Processing Assistants in the Pay
and-Z (9300-348 ith Grade Pa s4600/- as on 20161

EPF Organization ~ regarding.

The matter of preparation of Seniority List of Data Processing Assistant (DPA) has
been pending since creation of the post of DPA and notification of the Recruitment Rules of
the post of DPA. In accordance with the decision of the 65" Executive Committee, CBT all
the existing DEOs who were found eligible for conversion in accordance with the
Recruitment Rules were placed in the new grade of DPA and those converted in relaxation
of RRs were also placed as DPA subsequently. The existing DEOs were holding three
different grades in different scales of pay namely Grade”A”", Grade”B” and Grade “C” in
accordance with the Recruitment Rules notified for these grades at the time of conversion
as DPA ,when Data Entry Operators were recruited, an all India Seniority List was being
followed. An all India seniority list of Data Entry Operators as on 31.03.2003 has been
issued vide letter no. HRM.HI/1(3)99/DEO/Seniority/Pt./41878-904 dated 01.10.2004.

2. In the 54* meeting of the EC held on 06.12.2005,it was approved to reallocate the
sanctioned 447 posts of DEOs in the ratio of 40:40:20 (40% posts of Grade C, 40% posts of
Grade B, 20% posts of Grade A). The new ratio of the grades of DEOs ie. Grade ‘A’, 'B’ &'C’
were introduced to remove stagnation with different lengths of service prescribed for
placement. At this stage, the seniority was made on the regional basis and the promotions
to various grade i.e. ‘A’, ‘B’ & ‘C’ were effected by each region in accordance with the
available vacancies subject to the officials fulfilling the eligibility conditions. This was
communicated to Regional Offices vide letter No.
HRM.IIT/1(3)99/DEO/Seniority/Pt.1/20294 dated 04.12.2006.

3. Subsequently, during the year 2009, a comprehensive proposal was placed before
the 65" EC held on 22.02.2009 to restructure the existing posts in the IS Division, A new
Grade of DPA in higher Pay Scale (Rs. 6500-10500) (pre-revised) was created. As per the
Recruitment Rules for DPA notified on 30.05.2009, the incumbents who had rendered six
years regular service as DEO/ Supervisor (Computer Cell) / Assistant Programmer and
possessing the educational qualifications prescribed in the RRs were deemed converted
from the date of notification of the RRs i.e. 30.05.2009, As a one time measure, an initial
relaxation to the RRs was introduced providing that all the existing DEOs who were halding
the grades of ‘A’, ‘B’ & ‘C’ and did not possess the minimum educational qualifications will
be appointed on regular basis, on acquiring minimum educational qualifications within a
period of two years from the date of Notification of Recruitment Rules. The DPA was

allotted pay band of PB-2 (9300-34800) with grade pay of Rs. 4200. This was later changed
to the grade pay of Rs. 4600 vide Head Office letter No. HRD/1(2)/2008/Implementation 6"
CPC/5272 dated 19.05.2010. With the creation of new entry cadre of DPAs and conversion
of all eligible DEOs possessing eligibility of service & educational qualifications and also
those who acquired educational qualification in relaxation of the Recruitment Rules, a single
cadre of DPA is existing as of now. Therefore, the seniority list is to be published on All
India basis as the DPA is envisaged as an All India cadre similar to the category of officers in
the same grade pay in EPFO.

Subject: Provisional Seniority List of Assistant Provident Fund

of Rs. 5400/- as on 01.01.2016 in the EPF Organization - reg.

A provisional seniority list in the cadre of Assistant Provident Fund
Commissioner was circulated vide Office Order No. HRM-II/S.1(1)2013/29164-378
dated 17.01.2013 by taking into account all the DP candidates available upto
31.12.2012 and objections were invited for consideration within 30 days from the date
of issue of the said order i.e. after 17.01.2013. In response as many as 23
objections were received and examined upto 25.06.2013,

2. Some more officers were made available to be appointed against the
promotion quota as per the recommendations in sealed cover opened on exoneration
from the charges on conclusion of Departmental Proceedings. This necessitated
further updation of the said provisional seniority to include al! such APFCs who were
regularly appointed against the promotion quota prior to 31.12.2012 which was
further circulated vide this office order No. HRM-II/S-1(1)2013 dated 20.01.2014 and
a further time of 30 days further were given for receiving objections. As many as 12
objections were received from the concerned officers in addition to the 23 objections
received earlier. Due to administrative reasons, the finalization of revised provisional
seniority list circulated on 20.01.2014 was delayed. However, the objections were
disposed off after examination by 17.06.2015 and the said seniority list of APFCs as
on 31.12.2012 was approved by the competent authority on 14.07.2015 and
circulated vide this office letter No. HRM-II/S-1(1)2013/16649 dated 16.07.2015 in
accordance with EPF Staff (Fixation of Seniority) Regulation, 1989 which is based on
the principles contained in Department of Personnel and Training, Government of
India, Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pension O.M, No. 35014/2/80
Estt.(D) dated 07.02.1986 and OM No. 22011/7/86-Estt(D) dated 03.07.1986.

Personnel, Public Grievances and Pension has issued detailed instructions vide their
OM No. 22011/1/2012-Estt.(D) dated 04.03.2014 after examination of the decision of
the Hon’bie Supreme Court of India in N.R. Parmar & Others versus UOIL and in
consultation with the Department of Legal Affairs, Government of India on the
principles to be followed in the fixation of seniority between DR and DP candidates.
It has been made clear in the said DOP&T OM dated 04.03.2014 that the principles for
determination of inter se seniority of direct recruits and promotees wouid be effective
from 27.11.2012 i.e., the date of Supreme Court Judgment in Civil Appeal No. 75147515/2005 in the case of N.R. Parmar Vs. UOI & Ors” and the cases of seniority

4. EPFO was not a party to the case before the Hon'ble Supreme Court in NLR,
Parmar & Others Vs. UOI nor does it directly relates to EPFO. The instructions
stipulated in the DoP&T circular dated 04,03.2014 issued pursuant to the above
Judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court only are applicable to the EPFO from the date

of issue,

sufficient for the purpose of applying the relevant clause of DOPT circular dated

Subject Conversion of Data Entry Operators (Gr-A)/(Gr-B)/ (Gr-C) to the post of Data
Processing Assistant - Grant of pay structure of Grade Pay of Rs. 4,600/- in
Pay Band-2 notionally from 30.05.2009 - drawal of excess of Pay etc. and
recovery thereof - regarding.

Dear Sir,

This is with reference to the following instructions issued from Head Office on the modalities to
be adopted in connection with conversion of Data Entry Operators, Grade-A/B/C to the post of Data
Processing Assistant from 30.05.2009 and thereafter:

a) HRM. III/1(3)2009/DPA/18838 dated 24.09.2009 (Copy attached)

b) HRM.III/1(3)2009/DPA/19548 dated 13.10.2009 (Copy attached)

Cc) HRD/4(1)2009/Misc/circular/8885 dated 23.11.2009 (Copy attached)

d) HRD/1(2)2008/Implementation of 6" CPC/5721 dated 19.05.2010 (Copy attached)
e) HRM.V/14(2)2010/Pay Fix./DPA/16236 dated 21.06.2010 (Copy attached)

f) HRM.V/1(5)2010/DPA/Pay Fix./Pt./27857 dated 17.12.2012 (Copy attached)

g) HRM.V/1(5)2010/DPA/Pay Fix./Pt./1127 dated 15.04.2013 (Copy attached)

2, The Recruitment Rules of the Data Processing Assistants were notified in the Official Gazette of
India on 30.05.2009. The method of recruitment was 100 % direct recruitment. But as one time
relaxation on cadre restructuring, the existing Data Entry Operators (Gr-A)/(Gr-B)/(Gr-C) possessing the
minimum educational qualifications with 6 years regular service shall be deemed to have been appointed
from the date of notification. Further as one time relaxation, the existing Data Entry Operators (GrA)(Gr-B)(Gr-C) who do not Possess the minimum educational qualifications will be appointed on regular
basis only on acquiring the minimum educational qualifications within two years from the date of
notification of the said Recruitment Rules.

“s All those Data Entry Operators (Gr-A)/(Gr-B)/(Gr-C) who were having requisite qualifications and
years of regular service as on 30.05.2009 were converted to Data Processing Assistants and such
conversion was effective from the date of notification of the Recruitment Rules of DPA and only on

4. On the basis of the instructions issued by Government of India, Ministry of Finance Department
of Expenditure Office Memorandum - F. No. 1/1/2008-IC dated 13.11.2009 circulated vide this office
letter No. HRD/4(1)2009/circular/8885 dated 23.11.2009, clarification was issued to field offices vide this
letter No. HRD/1(2)2008/Implementation of 6” CPC/5721 dated 19.05.2010 by which pay Structure of
Grade Pay of Rs. 4,600/- in PB-2 was allowed to the Data Processing Assistants in the pre-revised scale
of Rs. 6,500-10,500 w.e.f. 30.05.2009 who were granted the normal replacement pay structure of Grade
Pay of Rs. 4,200/- in the PB-2 (Rs. 9,300-34,800).

<2 Representations were received from different regions seeking clarification on grant of Grade Pay
of Rs. 4,600/- to the Data Processing Assistants having pre-revised scale of Rs. 6,500 -10,500 w.e.f.
30.05.2009. The representations were examined and in accordance with the instructions and circular as
referred to at Para 4 above, the Competent Authority granted the Grade Pay of RS. 4,600/- in place of

Rs. 4,200/- w.e.f. 30.05.2009 vide letter No. HRD/1(2)2008/Implementation of 6” CPC/5721 dated
19.05.2010.

6. The references continued to be received from field offices regarding fixation of pay of the Data
Entry Operators (Gr-A)/(Gr-B)/(Gr-C) on conversion to the post of Data Processing Assistant.
Clarifications were issued in reply to a query raised by RPFC, West Bengal on fixation of pay stating
therein that the pay of the DPA need to be fixed w.e.f. 30.05.2009 i.e. from the date of notification of
Recruitment Rules of DPA and in accordance with FR 22(1)(a)(2) which stipulates that when the
appointment to the new post does not involve such assumption of duties and responsibilities of greater
importance, he shall draw as initial pay, the Stage of the time-scale which is equal to his pay in respect of
the old post held by him on regular basis, or, if there is no such stage, the next stage above in respect of
the old post held by him on regular basis. Meaning thereby, the DEOs who were placed as DPA on
conversiot: can only get the pay band pay drawn by them in the lower post and the grade Pay should be
changed from Rs. 4,200/- to Rs. 4,600/- . The Grade Pay of Rs. 4,600/- was to be allowed from
30.05.2009 or from the date the DEOs acquired requisite qualification and completed six years of regular
service, as the case may be and financial benefit was to be allowed only from the date they assumed
charge as DPA.

7 References were further received from field offices seeking clarification regarding pay fixation on
conversion of Data Entry Operators (Gr-A)/(Gr-B)/(Gr-C) to the post of Data Processing Assistant. The
same were examined in Head Office in consultation with the Audit Wing and the following were clarified :

a) The DEOs who were eligible for appointment/conversion as on the date of notification of the
Recruitment Rules of DPA are allowed the pay of DPA notionally from 30.05.2009 i.e. the date of
notification of RRs and with financial benefits from the date of assumption of charge.

b) The DEOs who were subsequently appointed to the post of DPA consequent upon acquiring
required educational qualification within a period of two years are allowed the pay of DPA from
the date of assumption of charge to the post of DPA.

8. The clarification regarding fixation of Pay on conversion of Data Entry Operators (Gr-A)/(GrB)/(Gr-C) to the post of Data Processing Assistant were further issued vide this office letter No.
HRM.V/1(5)2010/DPA/Pay Fix./Pt./1127 dated 15.04.2013 wherein it was clearly mentioned that the
issue of grant of 3% increment in pay fixation to DPAs on their conversion from DEOs is not permissible
as it is only a conversion not a promotion.

9. In view of the above clarifications, it is reiterated that the Data Entry Operators who have been
converted to Data Processing Assistant are not entitled to increment @ 3% either on 30.05.2009 or on
acquiring requisite qualification with six years regular service by 30.05.2011 as the case may be and the
financial benefit is only admissible from date of assumption of charge as DPA.

10. Inspite of the above, certain field offices treating the conversion as promotion or direct
recruitment had allowed increment initially from the date of notification 30.05.2009 or on acquiring
qualification of 6 years regular service and arrears of Grade Pay from the date of notification. This is
highly irregular,

11. In view of above, it is directed that the implementation of the 7" pay revision to such DPAs who
have received excess payments will be done only after regularising the excess payment made. The
excess pay drawn be recovered forthwith and in one lumpsum from the arrears of the pay due to them
from 01.01.2016 to 31.07.2016 on implementation of the recommendations of 7‘ Pay Commission. If
the amount of arrears falls short of the recoveries to be made, the same should be recovered from the
revised pay of August, 2016.
