Subject : Exemption under Section 17(1)(a) of the EPF & MP Act, 1952 and under Para 27A of the
EPF Scheme, 1952 —- Regarding.
Sir,
References are being received in the Head Office seeking clarification whether Income Tax
Recognition Order is one of the requisite documents to be submitted by the establishments seeking grant of
exemption from operation of the EPF Scheme, 1952.

2. Vide Head Office circular No. C-Il/Misc./2/06/EZ/Ex. /79520-79690 dated 28.12.2007, on the subject
cited above, elaborate guidelines to be followed by the field offices for processing proposals for grant of
exemption of the establishments from operation of the EPF Scheme, 1952 and forwarding the same to the
Head Office had been issued. The aforesaid circular is available on the official website of EPFO at serial No.
20 under Office Orders / Circulars (Old Circulars). Paragraph 8. of the aforesaid circular mentions the
essential information/documents/certificates which should accompany an exemption proposal forwarded to
Head Office. Point No. (xiii) of paragraph 8. of the circular mentions Income Tax Recognition Order as one of
the essential documents (for Provident Funds which came into existence before 31.03.2008).

3. The issue has been examined and it is felt that benefits of Income Tax provisions can be availed only
after the Trust is recognized by the Income Tax authorities, and EPF authorities are concerned only with the
benefits available under the EPF & MP Act, 1952 and the Schemes framed thereunder. However, if the Trust
does not get recognition under Income Tax Act after grant of exemption, then the employees of the
establishment will be getting overall less benefits as compared to employees of un-exempted establishments.
Therefore, in order to remove difficulties and also to ensure that overall benefits to the employees of the
exempted establishments are not less favourable, it is clarified that henceforth instructions contained in
paragraph 8, of the aforesaid Head Office circular dated 28.12.2007 stands modified to the extent that point
No. (xiii) of paragraph 8. of the circular may please be considered as omitted. Other things remain the same.

4. In view of above, henceforth, field offices will not ask the establishments seeking grant of exemption
from the operation of the EPF Scheme, 1952 to furnish of copy of Income Tax Recognition Order as an
essential document to be submitted with proposals for grant of exemption. However, immediately after grant
of exemption by the appropriate Government, the establishment should get recognition from the Income Tax
authorities for its Trust.

rightly reflecting the branch in its returns. The Regional PF Commissioner concerned has sought necessary
guidelines from Head Office to deal with the Situation.

establishments, only the main establishment exempted/relaxed by order is required to file online returns, the
branches/units of such exempted/relaxed establishments are not expected/required to file the online returns.
Details of branches/units having separate code or branches/units not having separate codes are being
furnished by the main establishment in its returns. If branches/units of exempted establishments are allowed

Trusts, etc. being captured through returns.

been erroneously covered under Section 1(3)(a), instead of having been covered under Section 2A as a
branch, necessary corrigendum to coverage letter/note may be issued and establishment details in the
establishment master of the office may also please be suitably corrected. Further, link for filing online returns
made available to such branches/units of exempted/relaxed establishments should also be withdrawn

Subject
: Implementation of the recommendations of the 7th Central Pay
Commission as accepted by the Government of India and as adopted by
the Central Board - generation of salary in the Revised Pay Structure
from August, 2016 and payment of arrears thereof – regarding.

Dear Sir,




The Government of India, Ministry of Finance, Department of Expenditure vide Resolution No
1-2/2016-IC dated 25.07.2016 (copy enclosed) accepted the recommendations of the 7th Central Pay
Commission on Minimum Pay, Fitment Factor, Index of Rationalization, Pay Matrixes and general
recommendations on pay without any material alterations. The same was brought to the notice of
the Central Board of Trustees, EPF in their 214th meeting held on 26.07.2016. The Central Board
adopted the notification on resolution of the Government of India accepting the 7th Pay
Commission's recommendations . The Central Board also resolved to adopt any other notification
that will be issued by the Government of India in due course for the Officers and employees of the
Central Board.

2.
The Government of India has further notified the Central Civil Services (Revised) Pay Rules,
2016 vide GSR No. 721(E) dated 25.07.2016 (copy enclosed) which shall be deemed to have come
into force on the 1st day of January, 2016 stipulating therein the method of fixation of pay in the
revised pay structure with effect from 01.01.2016.

3.
Further, Government of India, Ministry of Finance, Department of Expenditure vide their OM
No 1-5/2016-IC dated 29.07.2016 (copy enclosed) issued instructions on implementation of the
recommendations of the 7th Central Pay Commission - fixation of pay and payment of arrears. It has
also been stipulated that the salary for the month of August shall be paid in the revised pay
structure along with the arrears from 01.01.2016 to 31.07.2016.

4.
All the preparatory activities for payment of salary and arrears, consequent to the
implementation of 7th Central Pay Commission recommedations, need to be initiated. Since, the
salary and allowances are calculated through a software across the country since June, 2016,
necessary provisions in the Salary Module of HRSoft software are being made to enable the field
offices for calculation of salary and arrears. The preparatory activities include obtaining undertakings
in the prescribed “FORM OF OPTION” under Rule 6(2) of the CCS (RP) Rules 2016 from every
employee at the time of exercising option under Rule 6(1) which is mandatory before drawal and
disbursement of salary and arrears.

Page 2 of 2

5. As in HoSoft, some of the information like the income tax slab, contribution towards SPF etc.
are not available, the following exercise need to be taken by field offices immediately:

a) For SPF Deduction from Salary and Arrears, the minimum rate of contribution
prescribed (6% of pay) shall be deducted by the software wherever the deductions so made
is not meeting the minimum requirement.

b) For Income Tax Deduction, the slabs of deduction at the rate of 10% / 20% / 30% ,
whichever is applicable, need to be selected for each employee based on the income tax
slab in which he/ she falls.

c) The Data regarding status - Substantive / Officiating – need to be kept ready for each
employee for entry in the function once provision is made for generation of the “Statement
of Fixation” as per the prescribed format as annexed to the Office Memorandum dated
29.07.2016.

d) All Offices need to prepare the details ready in respect of all such employees, who are not to
be granted arrears with reasons.

e) All Offices need to keep the dates of such officials ready with full details whose salaries have
undergone a change since January, 2016 due to promotion , MACP, financial upgradation
etc. for the purpose of grant of increment as stipulated in the notifications who are not
entitled for increment as on 01.07.2016.

6.
Since the functions for “DA Arrear Date Entry”, “PAY Fixation as per 7th CPC” and ARREAR
Calculation for 7th CPC” will take some time for preparation, all offices may keep all data ready so
that action on the above functions can be taken immediately once the same are launched.

Sub: Inspection of Security/Manpower/ Facility Management
Establishments.

Madam / Sir,

Large number of establishments engaged in providing security services, supply
of manpower facility management establishments and construction companies are
covered under EPF & MP act 1952. Several complaints are received regarding
underreporting of employees/ contribution under the act in respect of such
establishments. Often, the nature of such complaints is that these establishments
have not enrolled all of the employees deployed with different principal employer/
clients.

Zi In this regard, it is observed that while inspecting compliance of such
establishments/ companies under EPF & MP Act, 1952 only absolute number of
employees are reported by field officers and this may not give correct picture about
number of employees engaged.

3. Hence, it has been decided that from now onwards (a.) it shall be mandatory
on the part of Enforcement Officers, to report numbers of employer in respect of
these security/manpower/facility management establishments with reference to each
of principal employer/clients being served by these establishments and (b.) In case
of any 7A proceeding, in respect of such establishments, it shall be mandatory on
the part of officers working as Departmental Representatives to report numbers of
employees in respect of these security/manpower/facility management
establishments with reference to each of the principal employers/clients being served
by these establishments.

4. Further, while carrying out inspection of principal employers it must be
ascertained whether the details of contract awarded have been uploaded by the
principal employer in the EPF portal and the same should be reported in the
inspection report. The Inspection Proforma (Unexempted Establishments) has
accordingly been modified with the inclusion of live items 2A & 7A in the proforma.
A copy of the modified Inspection Proforma is enclosed for ensuring that all future
inspections are firstly, carried out keeping the instructions in the circular in view, and
secondly duly reported in the revised proforma.

(This issues with the approval of CPFC)

Yours faithfully,

Subject :Benefit of two years weightage of service to the members with 20 or more
years of Pensionable Service under Employees’ Pension Scheme, 1995 ~
regarding.

Sir,

Various communications are being received from many ROs/SROs related to
the dispute on calculation of pensionable service for granting benefit of two years
weightage to the pensioners on completion of 20 years of pensionable service under
EPS, 1995. The issue was under consideration at Head Office in the light of disputes
raised at various legal forum. This mater was taken up with the Ministry of Labour &
Employment, Government of India.

Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government» of India vide its
communication no.S.65015/1/2013-SS-I| dated 06.07.2016 has accepted the
Proposal submitted by EPFO. As per the consent given by Ministry of Labour &
Employment, Government of !ndia benefit of two years weightage to the members
under EPS, 1995, with membership of 20 years or more under EPS, 1995 combined
with membership period under erstwhile Employees’ Family Pension Scheme 1971
should be taken into account.

Hence, it is decided that for granting the benefit of two years weightage
henceforth as well as for the cases settled, Pensionable Service will include service

. rendered under EPS 1995 as well as erstwhile Family Pension Scheme 1971 to fulfill
the condition of 20 year or more Pensionable service.

It is also requested that reply/report of compliance on the above line may be
filed before all the forums where dispute on the subject matter is pending for
decision.

eliminating the causes which lead to grievances and/or Court Cases. He advised that
pro measures may be taken for handling all stakeholders of the EPF so as to minimize
the grievances and complaints. CPFC also informed that enrollment of all workers
employed on contract or through contractors under EPFO, is a major issue being
examined by Parliamentary Standing Committee of Labour & Employment, as also
the Consultative Committee attached to the Ministry of Labour & Employment.
CPFC informed that he has written to Chief Secretaries of all the State Governments,
Heads of Central and State Government Public Sector Units, Banks and Railways to
ensure that all eligible contract workers are enrolled with EPFO. Further action may
be taken on the communication urgently.

2. CPFC emphasized the need for better use of technology to provide enhanced
services to members and establishments. He also emphasized to need for better
communication of EPF policies and benefits to stakeholders to promote the culture
of voluntary compliance. Enrollment of eligible employees in Building &
Construction Industries is a major area of and all efforts need to be taken through
possible channels to achieve this objcetive. Action to be taken by all Zonal ACCs.

3. ACC-HQ (RB) informed that enrollment of Construction Workers is not progressing
because of issues relating to enrollment of workers under EPF from the actual
retrospective date. He proposed that Compliance Wing of EPFO may issue detailed
instructions advising the EPF field offices that compliance from prospective date may
be ensured in all such cases. It was informed that a legal clarification for immediate
enrollment of current workers has been issued in respect of 7A inquiries to facilitate
enrollment of all existing workers. Action to be taken by ACC (Compliance).

4. CPFC informed that an advance search facility for UIDAI database has recently been
made available to EPF field offices. He directed that this facility may be made use of
for seeding Aadhaar data or for verifying genuineness. At this point, Shri Jagmohan,
ACC (IS) informed the officers that directions have been received from Prime
Minister Office, that Aadhaar details be captured in respect of currently contributing
members by 30th September, 2016. He further stated that there are 3.76 crore
average contributing members per month and digitally authenticated Aadhaar
number are available in respect of 1.21 crore members. He suggested that EPF field
offices may first identify large establishments having more than 50 contributing
members and focus on them for getting Aadhaar details. Action to be taken by all
Zonal ACCs.

5. CPFC advised Zonal ACCs to have regular meetings with establishments having large
number of contributing members and advised them to furnish Aadhaar in respect of

Subject: Procurement of Digital Signature Certificates (DSC) for
implementation of online APAR for Commissioners’ Cadre-regarding.

Sir/Madam,

This is in context of the SPARROW software of NIC which will be
introduced shortly for online APAR of EPFO officers. The implementation of
said software would require “Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)” of the officers
i.e. reportee officer, reporting officer and receiving officer. This requirement of
procuring DSC for officers in Commissioners” Cadre, i.e. APFC and above,
has been raised by HRM division of Head Office for the said purpose.

2. In connection to this requirement, all offices are hereby informed that
they can procure the Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) from NICSI at the
approved prices or from any other source, whichever they find convenient and
economical. A detailed instruction sheet of NICSI is appended with this letter.
Wherein, NICSI has mentioned the procedure to procure the digital signature.
The steps are reproduced below for convenience.

Step 1. Write an e-mail to nicsi-pi@nic.in mentioning a
requirement of “Class 3 DSC with token” (2 Years validity).

Step 2.NICSI will provide the Proforma Invoice and User
information Sheet. Concerned office should make the payment
mentioned in the Proforma invoice and fill the User Information
Sheet and send it to NICSI.

Step 3. Send the user information sheet to dscproj-nicsi@nic.in
and nicsi-pi@nic.in.

Step 4. After NICSI gets the payment and user information sheet
then it will be sent to empaneled vendor.

Step 5. The Vendor will come to collect the documents like
photograph, identity & address proof etc before servicing the
request.

Step 6. DSC and token will be issued to the concerned official.

2. All the offices can follow the above mentioned steps to get the digital
signatures for their officers.

4. This is a time bound activity so all offices are requested to get it
completed in shortest possible time. The procurement completion report
needs to be sent to HRM division as soon as the procurement gets completed
for all the officers present in the concerned office.

5. Accordingly all RPFCs-in-charge are requested to personally monitor
the issue to get the above task completed on priority basis.

Yours faithfully,

(V. Ranganath)

Subject:- Use of UAN- making it compulsory - Relaxation in the instructions for UAN on
claim forms —regarding.

Reference: Circular No. Coord./40(24)2010/DPG/Review meeting dated 17-12-2015.
(SLNo.551 in circulars of 2015-16 in EPFO website )
Sir/Madam,
Reference is invited to the circular cited above wherein instructions were issued in para — 2 of
the cited reference that with effect from 1‘ January, 2016, no claim form was to be accepted unless
Universal Account Number (UAN) was mentioned on the claim form.

2. Instances of difficulties being faced by members on account of the instructions have been
brought to notice particularly in respect of members who had ceased to be in employment before
01.01.2014 given the fact that initially UAN was allotted only to members who were subscribers
during January, 2014 to June, 2014. There could also be other cases and instances where insisting on
the requirement of UAN with the claim form may cause undue hardship to the claimant.

3. The matter has been, accordingly, reconsidered and it has been decided to relax the
instructions in partial modification of directions given in the referred circular as given below:-

i. Claim forms may be accepted without UAN if the date of leaving/exit of the member is before
01.01.2014.

ii. In exceptional cases, the officer-in-charge of the Regional/ Sub- Regional Offices may at their
discretion based on the merits of the case allow acceptance of claim forms without UAN.

(This issues with the approval of Central Provident Fund Commissioner.)

Yours faithfully,

Aw

Madam) Sir,
Please refer to the subject cited above.

2. Since the increment is due to be released in the month of July, RC{(NDC} has intimated that
the a new function “ Annual Increment Function” has been prepared for the calculation and
generation of salary for the month of July 2016. In the previous months the salary was generated
on or after the 1st of the new month if the salary for the previous month was approved. For
the month of the July, 2016, the “Generate Salary” will not happen until the following is done:

i. The Increment file is approved at the Administration Section (three level function:
Initiator/Verifier/Pre Audit).
ii. Based on the sanctioned Increment, the HRA part is to be corrected by the Salary Role
users (Two level: DA Salary/Verifier Salary).
lili. | Once these two are done, the “Generate Salary Function” will allow the generation of
the salary for July 2016 and then the process is same as of the previous months.

3. The step by step manual regarding action to be taken in rejiation to the above function
provided by NDC are enclosed as Annexure. It is requested that all offices should take
immediate steps to study the process and initiate action immediately. It is suggested that the
activities related to “Increment sanction part” may be completed by 08.07.2016 and the
activities related to “HRA Part” by 12.07.2016.

followed by the “Exact Function / User Role” in which the problem is being faced. Further,
on receipt of any clarification / guidance from NDC, a confirmation regarding the solution of
the problem may also be sent to the above email ids.

improvements in the Salary Module of HRSoft in order to make the software more use friendly

all suggestion regarding all the functions of Salary Module as on date may be sent by email
with scanned copy of formats etc attached along-with the enabling rule provisions for such
suggestion if any. It is also requested that all offices may forward the format being used for
NEFT file as some requests in this regard is also received. In order to take the consolidated
view of the same, all RPFC In Charge of Regions are requested that consolidated suggestions
on all issues including NEFT File Format may be compiled in respect of all the offices under
their jurisdiction and forwarded to this office by 18.07.2016 so that the same can be examined
by the software team and a decision taken.

The undersigned is directed to say that consequent upon coming into force
of the CCS(RP) Rules, 2008, which were notified on 29.8.2008 but are effective
from 1.1.2006, fixation of pay on promotion on or after 1.1.2006 is carried out as
per Rule 13 thereof. This Rule is invoked only in cases of promotion from one
Grade Pay to another in the revised pay structure.

2. In terms of Section i of Part-A of the First Schedule of the CCS(RP)
Rules, 2008, which provides for revised pay structure in the form of applicable
Pay Bands and Grades Pay corresponding to various pre-revised pay scales, certain
pre-revised pay scales have been merged in a common Grade Pay in the revised pay
structure w.e.f. 11.2006. In view of this, the posts in those pre-revised pay
scales which have been merged in a common Grade Pay w.e.f. 1.1.2006, are normally
required to be merged even if these posts constituted feeder and promotional
grades in the pre-revised pay structure.

3. However, in cases where such merger of feeder and promotional posts in
the wake of their having come to lie in the same grade pay has not taken place due
to administrative reasons and the posts continue to retain their promotional and
feeder character as per the relevant Recruitment Rules, this Ministry issued
instructions vide OM No. 10/2/2011-E.IIIA dated 7.1.2013 providing for fixation
of pay on promotion in such cases under Rule 13 of CCS (RP) Rules, 2008 subject
to the conditions laid down therein,

4. Now, instances have been brought to the notice of this Ministry where the
feeder and promotional posts have been merged in view of the merger of the prerevised pay scales applicable to the erstwhile feeder and promotional posts in a

Subject:- Recovery of Arrear Dues-regarding.

Sir,

During course of meeting of parliament standing committee on labour held on
10.06.2016, it was observed that categorization IR (Immediate realisable) and NIR
(Not immediately realisable) needs to be revisited again and analysis may be done for
proper classification thereupon. Till date only in cases where courts have granted stay,
cases under liquidation and in BIFR cases where establishment has been declared sick
and rehabilitation scheme is sanctioned, needs to be categorized as not immediately
realizable and in instalment cases only the current months instalment may be shown as
realizable and the rest of the amounts of recovery needs to be classified as NIR.

2. During course of discussion it revealed that there are many other establishments
which are now lying closed or whereabouts of certain establishments are not known
and recovery is outstanding which is shown under IR Category. Accordingly, analysis
of such establishments may be made immediately wherein, an establishment is now
lying closed or whereabouts are not known.

3. The data relating to immediately realisable arrears of such establishments may
be examined and the periodicity of pending RRCs_ be ascertained from the date of
RRCs for less than 3 years and above 3 years pendency .

4. The information after analysing the periodicity as above be sent to Head Office in
the following proforma for exempted as well as unexempted category separately.

Subject : Generation of Salary for the month of June 2016 only from the Salary Module of HRSoft —
reg.

Madam/ Sir,

Please refer to this office circulars no. CAT. 22(17)2015/HQ dated 12.04.2016
(website S! No. 30/2016-17), 13.04.2016 (website S| No. 35/2016-17), 29.03.2016 (website SI No.
56/2016-17) and 20.05.2016 (website SI No. 88/2016-17) regarding the action to be taken for
generation of salary from October 2015 to April 2016 through the salary module of HRSoft.

2. In this regard, as all offices are aware that the salary for the month of June 2016 was to be
generated and disbursed only from the Salary Module of HRSoft. it was for this reason that all offices
had been directed vide circular dated 20.05.2016 to forward the certificate regarding generation of
salary upto April 2016 and May 2016 from the Salary Module of HRSoft. Inspite of repeated
telephonic reminders and emails it is observed that only 61 offices have sent the certificate in the
prescribed format for April Salary and 19 offices have sent the certificate for May 2016. Further 5
offices are yet to complete salary for the month of April 2016 and 29 offices are yet to complete
salary for the month of May 2016. Detailed status of all offices is enclosed as Annexure }.

3. Accordingly, all Officers-In-Charge of offices are requested to take immediate action to
complete all the activities upto to the month of May 2016 and start generation of salary for the
month of June 2016 from the Salary Module of HRSoft. Those offices which are not in a position to
do the same should forward their request for special permission to continue with existing software
giving full details as to why the same is required. Copies of emails etc sent to NDC on problems being
faced may be forwarded alongwith the replies received so that such issues may be taken up for
consideration and consultation with NDC. It may be ensured that mere suggestions for improvement
in the software which is not preventing generation of salary and disbursement from the Salary
Module should be not be cited as a reason for either delay or cited as a problem.

4, The request letters stated above should reach this office by 17.06.2016. However, in
view of the fact that 96 offices have managed to generate the salary upto May 2016 from the Salary
module of HRSoft shows that the software is functioning and hence all Officers-In-Charge are

requested to ensuré that the salary for June 2016 is generated and disbursed timely without any
delay as per rules.

5. All Additional CPFC (Zones) are again requested to ensure that the offices under
their jurisdiction forward the certificates for the months of April and May immediately and the same
should be forwarded to H.O by ACC(Zone) after collecting from all the SRO/RO by today evening.

Yours faithfully,

Sub: Administrative Guidelines for Proceedings
Under Section 7A of The EPF & MP Act 1952.

Ref :( a).H.O.circular no.7 (1)2012/RCs RM dt.06.08.2014

(b) .H.O. circularIII/110001/4/3(7)MIS.C/2013Vol.1I1I/22147
dt.06.02.2016

Madam/Sir,

In continuation of head office circular dated
06.08.2014 and dated 06.02.2016 in the reference
cited, following guidelines; purely from
administrative side, for conducting proceedings under
section 7A of the EPF & MP Act is being issued.

It has been observed that in large number of
establishment, benefits envisaged under the schemes
framed under EPF & MP Act do not accrue to the
workers due to continued pendency of 7A proceedings
and protracted litigation j;especially in respect of
establishments where determination of dues for
several years are involved.

Hence for the purpose of uniformity and in the
interest of expeditious disposal of proceeding,
following guidelines are issued for adherence:

(a). Newly covered establishments with retrospective
date of coverage and where several years are involved
and the establishment has not yet commenced the
compliance, the proceeding under section 7A of EPF &
MP Act may be initiated for the current year and

1

which must be concluded within three months of issue
of 7A notice and a separate 7A enquiry may be
initiated to determine the dues for the period prior
to the current year.

(b). In respect of 7A enquiry for evasion of
membership and non enrolment of contract employees
where determination of dues for several years are
involved, the proceeding under section 7A of the EPF
& MP Act may be initiated for the current year; which
must be concluded within three months of issue of 7A
notice and a separate 7A enquiry may be initiated to
determine the dues for the period prior to the
current year.

(This issues with the approval CPFC)

Sub: - Review/follow up regarding CPGRAMS Portal grievances and proper
functioning of PRO! facilitation centres-reg.

SirfMadam,

During recent review meeting held on 09.06.2016 Additional Secretary
(MOL&E) has reiterated that the member/complainant in respect of grievances
received on CPGRAMS Portal should invariably be personally contacted over phone
to ensure that they are fully satisfied with the redressal of their gnevances. Hence in
this regard it may please be ensured that the Nodal Officer for public grievance/a
responsible officer should personally contact the member/complainant after redressal
of each grievance received on CPGRAMS Portal for confirmation of satisfactory
disposal of the grievance by the office concemed.

2. Further, it has been observed that the facilitation Centres manned by Public
Relation Officer in field offices are not functioning properly. Head Office is not only
often receiving complaints from the public but also carried out a random check about
functioning of PRO cell of various field offices. It was found that either phone calls
made to PRO Cell were not being picked up or were continuously going busy. It was
also found that in many cases the name and other details of the PRO like phone
number ete published in telephone directory on website were not correct. Members
have also complained that even when their calls are picked up they do not get
satisfactory reply and they are not being connected to senior officers for redressal of
their grievances.

3 lt may please be noted that these are serious issues conceming the image of
the organisation and requires urgent attention at higher level, Hence all RPFCs of
field offices and concerned Zonal ACCs are hereby requested to personally verify the
functioning status of PROs of all offices under their administrative jurisdiction and
take appropriate necessary measures to streamline the working. They are also
requested to visit the facilitation cantres and PRO area for random check more often
and speak to the visitors also for first-hand information and problems faced by them.
The officers and staff handling the grievances should be sensitized to deal with the
members and complainants in a more polite manner.

543 (E) Gazette Notification increasing benefits under the EDLI Scheme,
1976 dated 24.05.2016- reg.

Sir,

The Gazette Notification Issued by the Govt. of India referred above has brought
IMportant amendments whereby the benefits of EDLT Scheme have been increased to Rs
6,00,000/-,

2. With the above amendments in the EDLI Scheme, 1976 the Quantum of benefits will
be substantially increased, In order to ensure uniformity in the application of the Amendments,
all offices may note the follawing;-

(1) in sub-paragraph (3), for clause (i), the following shall be substituted, namely:-

“(I) the average monthly wages drawn (Subject to a maximum of fifteen thousand
rupees), during the twelve months Preceding the month in which he died, multiplied
by thirty times plus fifty per cent, of the average balance in the account of the
deceased in the Fund or of a Provident fund exempted under section 1? of the Act or
under paragraph 27or 27 A of the Employees’ Provident Funds scheme, 1952, as the
case may be, during preceding twelve months or during the period of his membership,
whichever is less, subject to a ceiling of one lakh and fifty thousand rupees, subject to
2 total ceiling of six lakh rupees”:

(2) in sub-paragraph (4), for the words, brackets and figures “sub-paragraph (1), (2)
or (3)", the words, brackets and figures” sub-paragraph (1) or (2)", shall be
substituted,

3. Necessary Amendments in the application software are being made by IS division, but
in the meantime EDLI claims will be regulated as mentioned in the paragraph above, As it is
an important Amendment you are requested to give wide publicity to the same,

4, All establishments under Your jurisdiction may be advised to ensure compliance under
the enhanced benefit, EDLI exempted establishments may also be informed that benefits must

be revised and

paid on the higher wage ceiling along with the amendments made for enhanced
benefit.

5; Publicity may be given through press releases, letters to Employers/Employees
Associations, e-mails, Regional EPFO websites etc.

(This issues with the approval of CPFC)
Yours faithfully,

(Dr.S.K. Thakur)

Circular

PDUNASS, formerly NATRSS had published the names of the training programmes for the
year 2016-2017, vide letter no. 13(34)/2016-2017/NATRSS/1873 dated 29.03.2016 (S. No. 768
[2015-2016] of office order in EPFOs website). Further, vide letter no. 13(34)/20162017/NATRSS/227 dated 20.05.2016 (S. No. 90 of office order in EPFOs website) the names of
the nominated officers also for each training ensure was published.

2s Inspite of the above, it is seen that the participation in the courses has seen a negative
trend. Instances abound wherein the nominated officers express their inability to attend at the
last moment. Also, there is no attempt on the part of the officers to ascertain the status of their
requests for exemption with PDUNASS. There have also been cases where the nominated
officers have not even sought for any formal exemption but have simply chosen not to attend
without any information whatsoever.

3: It is reiterated that the nominations for the training courses had been approved by the
CPFC/ Dean, PDUNASS and as such, any exemption from attending any course can be given only
at the level of CPFC. Therefore, any request for exemption should be addressed to CPFC and
sent to Director, PDUNASS who shall place the same before CPFC for an appropriate decision.

4. It is only after receipt of a communication from Director, PDUNASS clearly exempting the
officer should he or she not attend the course. In other words, merely sending a request for
exemption will not imply that the officer can choose not to attend,

The above instructions should be adhered to strictly and any deviation shall be an
invitation for appropriate adverse action.

(This issues with the approval of CPFC)

-P. Varghese)

SN Query and Answer

by two offices for October 2015 or same office has uploaded the data twice
for the same EID? |
ANS © Once two or more the offices have uploaded the data of same person
for the Month of October 2015, it means that apart from one office which
‘| may be correct as Salary for that month was disbursed by that office, the
other offices have made error in uploading the same as regular salary bill for
the person must have been made by one office only.
© While processing the data the system will throw error saying that
there are duplicates and the list of the EID found more than once will be

© The user should use the Add/Edit Salary function and resolve the

office can process the data.

In case the data was uploaded by two offices for same employee and before

then how to handle the case?

© In such case if it is found that one office has already approved the
salary file means that the office has made error and not verified the data
properly.

© In such case the Salary if approved the data of all employees for those
Salary months and Subsequent months for which salary details are

verification is not proper and the approved file is wrong.

onwards.

3 How to handle a case when an employee has been transferred from one |

office to another?

o Once the employee has been transferred his details are to be added
in the office where he is posted. For this the following process will be there.
oOnce the salary for a month is approved all offices will generate the

data for the subsequent month in the first week of the month itself. The

Government of India is promoting the setting up of new Micro, Small and Medium
Enterprises (MSMEs) to catalyze the creation of employment opportunities through
them and therefore, various incentives and ease in regulatory compliance provisions are
being conceptualized for the MSMEs. In this connection, it is proposed now to simplify
and ease the compliance burden of these MSMEs under certain Labour Laws during
their initial 3 years of establishment with an inspection scheme taking into account the
self-certifying compliance with the Labour Laws. The Labour Laws to be covered under
this are:

(1) | The Industrial Disputes Act, 1947

(2) The Trade Unions Act, 1926

(3) The Building and Other Constructions Workers’ (Regulation of
Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1996

(4) The Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946

(5) The Inter-State Migrant Workmen (Regulation of Employment and
Conditions of Service) Act, 1979

(6) The Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972

(7) | The Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970

8) — The Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
(9) |The Employees’ State Insurance Act, 1948

2. It is observed that out of the 9 Central Labour Acts above, first 7 Acts are
implemented both by State Government (State sphere) and Central Government
(Central sphere). Last two (EPF and ESI Act) are mainly implemented by Central
Government. Also, out of these 7, only 4 Acts (viz. Industrial Disputes Act, Building &
Other Construction Workers Act, Inter-State Migrant Workmen Act, and Contract Labour
Act) require establishments to file Return. Similarly, only 4 Acts (viz Building & Other
Construction Workers Act, Inter-State Migrant Workmen Act, Payment of Gratuity Act
and Contract Labour Act) require inspection of the establishments by inspectors.

3. In order to promote the setting up of MSMEs to generate employment
opportunities through them, it is proposed to have an inspection scheme for the above
mentioned labour laws taking into account the self-certified returns filed by them,
provided the MSMEs are not more than 3 years old. MSMEs can self-certify compliance
through a combined single self-certified return under these laws. For MSMEs which are
less than 3 years old and have given a self-certified return mentioned above, the
inspection scheme may provide that only a small percentage of such units shall be
verified through a random risk based inspection system for compliance under the above

Subject: Workshop for Representatives of Exempted Establishments to be held
from 15-16 June, 2016- Inviting Nominations — Regarding.
Sir,

The Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya National Academy of Social Security has been
conducting Workshop for the Exempted Establishments on Employees’ Provident Fund
and Miscellaneous Provisions Act 1952 for the last several years.

The response for the programme from the industry has been quite encouraging and
almost all of the participants felt that such programmes should be conducted regularly to
inform the developments in EPF and EPS Administration.

As per the feedback of the participants in the earlier programs, and keeping in view the
recent developments in EPF and EPS Administration, the Academy has designed a two day
Workshop for Representatives of Exempted Establishments on 15-16 June,2016.

During the workshop following issues will be discussed:

Provisions of the EPF & MP Act, 1952 and the Schemes;

Key issues posing challenges in compliance;

Nature and periodicity of returns from exempted establishments
Processes and procedures for better coordination and cooperation
Investment pattern for provident funds.

Role of Employers for International Workers under the EPF&MP Act, 1952
Computerization in EPFO.

You are requested to collect 4-6 nominations from your regions for this workshop.

Keeping in view the requirement of Exempted Establishments and their interest to
participate in the programme, we have kept the participation fee for Residential participant @
Rs.5,000/- (Rupees five thousand only) per participant covering boarding and
lodging, course material etc. and Rs.4,000/- (Rupees Four Thousand only) per
participant for those not availing accommodation at PDUNASS, they will be given
study material and lunch.

Subject: Maintenance & repair of EPFO properties-reg.
Sir,

As you are aware that in accordance with the “Swachh Bharat Abhiyan”
already instructions have been issued emphasizing the need to keep office buildings
and staff quarter complexes neat and clean.

maintenance and cleanliness has not been found in offices and staff quarter
complexes. This issue was discussed during the recently held Review Meeting of
Zonal ACCs wherein it was informed by ACC(WB,NER & JHARKHAND) that CPWD is
not agreeing to take annul maintenance work of buildings constructed by it. Thereafter
this issue has been discussed with CPWD officers in the meeting held with CPWD and
NBCC on 5.5.2016 wherein officers from CPWD have assured that CPWD will
immediately take up annual maintenance work for all office buildings and staff quarter
complexes constructed by it.

3. Accordingly, it is once again advised that all OlCs must ensure timely
maintenance and cleanliness in their office premises and staff quarter complexes. The -
annual maintenance work in respect of office buildings and staff quarter complexes
shall be immediately given to CPWD wherever the office buildings and staff quarter
complexes have been constructed by CPWD.

4. Any non-cooperation from local CPWD office may immediately be brought to the
notice of undersigned and Shri V.K. Jayaswal, DDG(W),CPWD Nirman Bhawan, New
Delhi.

by CPWD, the maintenance work may be given to other agencies strictly in accordance
with the provisions in GFR & Schedule of Administrative & Financial

Powers of EPFO. If the ACC, Zone/RPFC-I of the region/RPFC-II, OIC, SRO are of the
view that there is need to bring some change in the existing delegation of
Administrative & Financial Powers appropriate changes may please be suggested
through proper channel so that the same may be recommended to concerned ACCIi(HRD) for immediate action.

6. The ACCs(Zones) shall be fully responsible for proper upkeep and maintenance

of office building and staff quarters in their zones and shall submit their report after
completion of requisite actions within one month i.e. on or before 6t June 2016.

Sir,

The Sub-Committee of the Executive Committee, CBT, EPF on Building &
Construction in its meeting No.1 held on 2"4 March 2016 noted the present status of on
going construction projects and decided that proper monitoring of the projects must be
ensured for timely completion ensuring quality and full compliance of relevant rules and
regulations including the provisions of EPF & MP Act, 1952 in respect of construction
workers engaged on the projects.

. This issue was also discussed in a meeting held with CPWD and NBCC on

5.5.2016 at Head Office wherein the CPWD officers informed that the rules and
procedures to be followed for execution of construction projects are already laid down
in GFR Rules 133. The relevant rule is reproduced as under:

Rule 133: For original works and repair works entrusted to a ‘Public Works
Organisation’ as defined in Rule 126(2), the administrative approval and
expenditure sanction shall be accorded and funds allotted by the concerned
authority under these rules and in accordance with the delegation of Financial
Power Rules 1978. The Public Works Organisation shall then execute the work
entrusted to it in accordance with the rules and procedures prescribed in that
organization.

Accordingly, all ACCs(Zones) are requested to constitute a Project Monitoring
Committee to be chaired by ACC(Zone) with RPFC-I of the Region, RPFC-II(FA) of
the Region and technical staff i.e. JE/AE of Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation
in the Region/Zone as members. The OIC of the SRO may also be co-opted, if
required. The Committee in accordance with Rule 133 of GFR may ensure that
execution of the work by the PWO is being done in accordance with Rules and
Procedures prescribed in the PWO. As the PWO in most of the cases is CPWD, the
CPWD Manual available on net, may please be referred to by the Committee. Any
gaps and irregularities noticed may be immediately taken up with the PWO for course
correction.

Subject:- E-Sameeksha for Performance monitoring and evaluation.
Sir,

The Hon’ble Chairman, Central Board (EPF) and Union Labour & Employment Minister
inaugurated the “e-Sameeksha” for use in the Employees’ PF Organisation on 15t May 2016 on the
occasion of ‘Labour Day’. This portal shall eventually become the primary monitoring tool for
performance review in EPFO. It has following salient features:-

i. It is a web based utility and can be accessed from any web connected device by
inputting specified user credentials.

ii. The default log-in id would be the official mail id on the epfindia.gov.in domain. All
incumbent Divisional heads in EPF Headquarters, Director (NATRSS), Zonal ACCS and
RPFCs in charge of field offices and Zonal Training Institutes may activate their email
ids, if not already activated. Passwords have been sent to the respective email ids,
which may be changed by the user.

iii. Action points arising out of decisions in various meetings will be available in a single
window interface.

iv. User privileges based on functional and positional hierarchy will control the access to
specific points on which “action taken and subsequent follow up action” is to be
notified.

Vv. Action points of meetings of Central Board (EPF), Executive Committee (CBT, EPF) and

various sub-Committees of the Board and EC and review meetings of Zonal
ACCs/RPFCs taken by CPFC shall be on e-Sameeksha portal. This list will be modified
in future as required.

2; Each Divisional head in EPF Headquarters, Zonal ACC and RPFCs in-charge of field offices
shall compulsorily access the E-Sameeksha portal once daily for further follow-up action.

Sub: Timely and Quality Redressal of Public Grievances in CPGRAMS / EPFIGMS
Portals - Reg.

Sir,

You are well aware that the public grievances in respect of all government
departments are being monitored by the Hon'ble Prime Minister of India through
PRAGAT| meetings held every month and e-Samiksha Portal of Government of India
The PRAGATI e-Samiksha portal is also covering grievances related to EPFO. The
Hon'ble Prime Minister has desired that all possible efforts should be made for speedy
and quality disposal of public grievances.

2. From time to time instructions have been issued earlier for streamlining the entire
process of grievance redressal and its monitoring in EPFO which are required to be
meticulously followed.

3. However, it is once again advised that all the grievances received by post,
telephone, email or in person ete must be registered on EPFIGMS on the same day of
their receipt in the respective office.

4. Each office has to closely monitor that not only the grievances are registered on
the same day but also to ensure that they are resolved at the earliest and reply is
updated on the portal after resolution of each grievance.

3: Please note that it is the responsibility of the concerned OIC to ensure that all
grievances are timely disposed, The quality of reply furnished in respect of each
grievance is also to be evaluated before uploading on the EPFiGMS/CPGRAMS portal
within one day of receipt of reply. All OlCs should dedicatedly monitor the quality

of disposal of grievance and evaluate the same before uploading the same on the
concerned portal so that a relevant and comprehensive reply is made available to the
member/complainant.

6. In case final reply is not possible, then an interim reply must be uploaded and
efforts shall continue to ensure expeditious final disposal to completely resolve the
grievance to the satisfaction of the concerned member/complainant.

tr. It has been observed that consistency of reply to the grievance Is often changed
during the course of redressal and a new direction to the issue is brought forward. This
should be avoided. It gives an impression that the grievances are not carefully perused
leading to furnishing of inconsistent status and reply.

8. Besides uploading the disposal on the EPFIGMS/CPGRAMS portal, the member
should also be informed by email/phone or by speed post where ever grievances have
been received in offline mode and where email/phone number is not mentioned.

9. After disposal of each grievance, it is imperative that the feedback of the
membercomplainant is obtained .The same should be examined to analyse whether
individual or systemic lapses have taken place in the entire process of grievance
redressal so thal corrective measures are taken to ensure that such lapses are not
repeated in future.

10. Although online redressal systems viz. CPGRAMS & EPFIGMS have
considerably facilitated the grievance redressal machinery in EPFO, these systems can
function optimally and effectively only if persons using the same exhibit sincerity of
purpose and effectiveness of action. For this, all senior officers have to take active
interest in ensuring the quality of disposals for grievances being received in EPFO via
different modes.

11. The RPFC-|, RO/Officer-in-charge of SRO should conduct regular and frequent
review of the grievance redressal mechanism in their respective offices. ACC (Zanes)
shall also review the working of the grievance redressal mechanism during their visit to
offices under their jurisdiction and incorporate the same in their visit notes.

12. Whereever necessary disciplinary action should be taken against officials found
responsible for causing inordinate delay/obstacle in the process of grievance resolution.

13. The RPFCs in charge of RO/SRO should also ensure that the PRO system in
their offices is working properly and effectively during the working hours and under no
circumstances it should be left unmanned, The phone calls must be attended in
courteous’ and helpful manner with due diligence.

Subject : Launching of Salary Module in the HRSoft { Software for HR Management) — addition of
new functions for salary generation — reg.

Madan) Sir,

Please refer to this office letter no. CAT. 22(17)2015/HQ dated 23.03.2016 (website St
No. 763/2015-16), 12.04.2016 (website Si No. 30/2016-17) and 13.04.2016 (website SI No. 35/201617) on the subject cited above.

2. In this regard, it is to intimate that based on the instructions already issued, action has been
taken by many offices for preparing the salary file for the salary details of October 2015 and uploading
the same. Further, such offices have also generated the “Check List of Errors” in the uploaded file if
any. Offices have also collected and uploaded the “Bank Details” of the employees based on which
the NEFT files will be generated where bank details are available and where the same are not available,
the cases will be processed for Cheque payment.

3. The required functions have now been provided in the Salary Module of HRSoft for taking the
next step towards the preparation of salary for the month of October 2015 till April 2016. The details
as prepared by IS Division regarding the functions and detailed process for carrying out the activities
are annexed as ANNEXURE A. The Detailed USER MANUAL will be available for download in the Login
of each User as provided by IS Division. The functions in brief are as under : -

(i) ADD / EDIT SALARY DETAILS FUNCTION

The basic use of this function is to edit the salary details of individual EIDs which are in the check list,
add EID if any missing and enter details, correct totalling mistake through “Add / Update” button, stop
salary of particular employee, add details under Other Payment Options , Other deductions, LIC, Postal
Life Insurance and Cooperative Society etc.

{il} PROCESS SALARY FUNCTION

After correcting all the errors in the “October Salary File” as given in the “Checklist Of Errors” through
the EDIT SALARY FUNCTION, the “DA-SALARY” can use this function to forward to “VERIFIER-SALARY”.

Page 1 of 6

“VEREFIER-SALARY” can approve the same and forward to “PAC-SALARY” or return for correction to
“DA-SALARY” for correction. Similarly “PAC-SALARY” may also approve and forward “CASH-SALARY”
or return to “DA-SALARY” for correction. “CASH-SALARY” can also approve or return to “DA-SALARY”
for correction. The process to be followed is same once it is returned to “DA-SALARY” for correction.
On approval by “CASH-SALARY”, the bills for subsequent month can be generated and there will be no
change in the approved bill after that.

(iii) GENERATE SALARY FUNCTION

This function can be operated once the salary for the month of October 2015 is approved by “CASHSALARY” and it will allow the generation of the next month’s salary details ie November 2015. The
data given for the October 2015 salary will be used by the software to generate the Salary for
November 2015. “DA-SALARY” will have to use the “Edit Salary Function” to make changes where
required jike stopping salary of persons left, changing the salary details for persons on promotion etc,
adding employee for transfer in or new appointments etc and follow the same process i.e. EDIT Salary
> Process Salary > Generate Salary for the subsequent months. The system will calculate the DA
as per revised rate while generating the Salary for April 2016 and also the NPS deductions.

{iv) ADD / ASSIGN BILL FUNCTION

This function will enable offices which generate multiple bills for salary of employees to generate the
bills for salary payment. However, since the salary for the month of October 2015 to March 2016 is on
test basis, single bill generation facility has been provided. However, once the salary for the month of
April is generated in the Module, the User will have to add the Bill Numbers — one by one to various
employees or in bulk. Default bill number for April shall be BILL- 042016. The details of the actions to
be taken are given in the ANNEXURE A.

(v} REPORTS FUNCTION

A number of reports have been provided to help in the preparation of the Salary fram October 2015
onwards. These reports are available in the Roles of DA Salary, Verifier Salary, PAC and CASH SALARY
Roles. The details are given in the “Annexure A”. The basic purpose of the various reports are to enable
viewing the salary details payment head wise, cadre/ designation wise, compare salary for two months
etc. The other reports namely the upload file for Income Tax, NPS, are under development.
Also the reports for the forwarding of the cheque to different offices against deducted
advance is under development.

4. All the Officers- In Charge are requested to ensure that the action to generate the salary from
the month of October 2015 to April 2016 is taken and the instructions issued vide circular dated
13.04.2016 is complied with.

Yours faithfulty,

Sir,

Please find enclosed herewith a letter of Sh. Subhash Kumar, received in this office on
26.04.2016, through online for seeking information under the Right to Information Act. The Copy of the
letter is forwarded to you for necessary action under the Right to Information Act, 2005. The information
has to be provided directly to the applicant under intimation to the undersigned. It is certified that the
applicant has deposited the application fee i.e. Rs.10/-

Ifthe desired information does not pertain to the concerned division or some part of information
is held by other division or public authority, the concerned CPIO shall forward /transfer the application
or such Part of it as may be appropriate to relevant division/Public authorities u/s 5(4) and 6(3) of the
RTI Act, 2005 respectively and inform the applicant immediately/about such transfer. However, if the
CPIO is not able to find out as to which division/ public authority is concerned with the information even
after making reasonable efforts to find out the concerned division/public authority to which the
application could be transferred. It would, however, be the responsibility of the CPIO, if an appeal is made
against his decision, to establish that he made reasonable efforts to find out the particulars of the
concerned division, public authority.

If some part of the information is the concern of a public authority under any State Government
or the Union Territory Administration, the CPIO receiving the application should inform the applicant that
the information may be had from the concerned State Government/UT Administration. Application, in
such a case, need not be transferred to the State Government/UT Administration,

Name & Address of the Appellate Authority may also be mentioned in the reply, so that the
applicant can make an appeal within 30 days from the expiry of such period or from the receipt of
decision given by the public authority, if he is aggrieved by the decision.

Subject: Monitoring of coverage of construction workers — Observing the Months of
April 2016 & May 2016 as “Compliance for construction workers” monthsregarding

Sir,

The matter of coverage of construction workers under the EPF & MP Act 1952 is
being monitored at the highest level in Government and is an area of utmost concern. On
the issue, assurances have also been given to Parliament that the coverage of construction
workers will be fully secured and the number of construction workers covered shall be
doubled.

However, in spite of repeated instructions, performance in this work area is still
below expectations. Therefore it has been decided that the months of April, May & June
2016 shall be observed as “Compliance for Construction Workers” months.

Accordingly, as already reiterated time and again vide various circulars, the work
may be accorded top priority and taken up in right earnest duly engaging the stakesholders
including various trade unions and other associations/bodies, Building & Construction
Workers Welfare Board in the State etc. The matter also needs to be followed up with the
Principal Secretary/Secretary Labour in respective States. Also, the recent facility provided
for capturing details of contracts awarded by the principal employer needs to be utilized to
ensure full compliance in respect of contractual employees also.

Since the coverage of construction workers needs to be at least doubled, the officewise targets have been worked out reflecting the minimum number of construction workers
which must be enrolled in respect of individual RO/SRO by the end of 30" June, 2016
without fail.

To ensure immediate action at operational levels and effective monitoring at
supervisory levels, a check list of major actions to be taken by OICs of RO/SRO is enclosed
herewith. The actions listed in the check list shall be completed by 29" April, 2016 and the

Contd...2

se A

check list duly filled in and signed by the OIC of RO/SRO shall be submitted to Zonal ACCs
who shall take further follow up action from their end so as to achieve the given target.

As the progress needs to be monitored at short intervals for initiating necessary
follow up action, a monthly progress report may be sent to the Head Office by the
respective Zonal ACC, the format of which is enclosed. The first monthly report as on 29"
April, 2016 may be submitted on or before 6" May, .2016 and the second monthly report as
on 31% May, 2016 may be submitted on or before 8" June, 2016, 3 monthly report as on
30" June 2016 may be submitted on or before 8" July, 2016. Only the consolidated report
from Zonal ACC shall be accepted at Head Office and OlCs of ROs/SROs must not send
any report directly to Head Office.

It is once again reiterated that OIC, SRO shall be fully responsible for attaining the
target for his office whereas OIC, RO shall be responsible not only for attaining the target
for his office but also for proper supervision of SROs under his jurisdiction for achievement
of this target. The overall supervisory responsibility shall lie with the Zonal ACC.

(This issues with the approval of Central Provident Fund Commissioner)
